<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:11pt><B>EXPLANATORY NOTE</B></FONT></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>This Amendment No. 1 on Form 10/A (this &#8220;Amendment&#8221;) amends and restates in its entirety the Registration Statement on Form 10 of Biointra, Corp. (the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;Biointra,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) originally filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on March 2, 2026 under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;) (Commission File No. 001-43172) (the &#8220;Original Filing&#8221;). This Amendment is being filed to:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>include our audited consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, for the year ended December 31, 2025 and for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024, together with the report thereon of Fruci &amp; Associates II, PLLC, our independent registered public accounting firm;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>include our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements as of June 30, 2026 and for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and update Item 2 (Financial Information) to discuss those interim periods;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>describe the acquisition by our subsidiary, Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (&#8220;BRA&#8221;), of four agricultural properties in the States of Jalisco and Nayarit, Mexico, in exchange for 1,500,000 shares of our Class A Common Stock, and the related critical audit matter and material weakness identified in connection with the audit of our 2025 financial statements;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>conform the capitalization, share issuance, beneficial ownership and related-party information to the audited and interim financial statements and to the records of our transfer agent;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>describe our letters of intent, our pending biomass supply arrangement, Amendment No. 1 to our Share Purchase Agreement with Silver Rock Group and our outlook for 2026 and 2027; and&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>correct the Commission file number, I.R.S. employer identification number and zip code shown on the cover page of the Original Filing, add the name of the exchange on which the Class A Common Stock is to be registered, and update the exhibit index.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our Class A Common Stock is not currently listed or quoted on any exchange or quotation system. On March 6, 2026, we submitted an application to list our Class A Common Stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (&#8220;Nasdaq&#8221;); the application is pending and Nasdaq has not approved it. We have applied to list under the proposed symbol &#8220;BCRP.&#8221; Based on our current stockholder base and financial condition, we do not yet satisfy Nasdaq&#8217;s initial listing requirements; see &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors &#8212;&nbsp;Risks Related to Our Securities.&#8221; Under Section 12(d) of the Exchange Act, the registration of our Class A Common Stock under Section 12(b) will become effective only after Nasdaq has approved our listing application and certified to the SEC that the Class A Common Stock has been approved for listing and registration. Until that time, we are not subject to the periodic reporting requirements of Section 13(a) of the Exchange Act. There can be no assurance that Nasdaq will approve our listing application. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors &#8212;&nbsp;Risks Related to Our Securities.&#8221;</P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>3</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 1. BUSINESS</B></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Corporate Information</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Biointra, Corp. is a Delaware corporation. Our Certificate of Incorporation was executed by our founder on May 8, 2024 and filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on May 10, 2024; our financial statements present our results from May 8, 2024 (inception). Our principal executive office is located at 1041 N. Dupont Hwy #1029, Dover, Delaware 19901, and our telephone number is +1 (302) 215-9097. Our operations are conducted in Mexico through our subsidiary, Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (&#8220;BRA&#8221;), a Mexican sociedad an&#243;nima promotora de inversi&#243;n de capital variable, in which we hold 99 of the 100 outstanding shares; the remaining share is held by our Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz, to satisfy the two-shareholder minimum under Mexican corporate law. BRA is consolidated in our financial statements as a wholly-owned subsidiary. Information on our website is not part of this Amendment.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Overview</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We are a development-stage company that is establishing treatment facilities for industrial organic waste, including the solid and liquid residues of tequila production, with the objective of converting these byproducts into renewable energy that can be incorporated into our customers&#8217; production processes. We develop renewable energy products and solutions and seek partnerships in renewable energy that are both environmentally sustainable and economically viable. Our mission is to provide recyclable energy solutions, renewable energy fuels and alternative electric power for small and mid-sized industrial users, initially in Mexico.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>To date, our efforts have concentrated on negotiations with prospective customers and the execution of non-binding letters of intent and confidentiality agreements, capital raising, organizational development, the launch of our website, the structuring of our business plan, the acquisition of BRA and the acquisition through BRA of four agricultural properties in Mexico. We have not generated any revenue since inception, we have no binding customer contracts, and we do not expect to generate revenue from waste-to-energy operations during 2026. Our independent registered public accounting firm has expressed substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8221; and &#8220;Item 2. Financial Information.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Our Solutions</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Biointra is an organization dedicated to delivering comprehensive energy solutions across diverse industries in Mexico. We intend to provide integrated solutions, from waste collection to energy generation, with the opportunity for clients to obtain &#8220;clean industry&#8221; certifications in Mexico and carbon credits without requiring additional investment. We intend to provide our solutions through two primary processes: solid energy solutions and liquid energy solutions.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our solid energy solution uses particle technology made available by our technology partners to valorize tequila bagasse, the fibrous solid residue produced in the tequila manufacturing process, by converting it into an industrial-grade biomass pellet. This pellet has been tested in steam generation for the production of tequila in industry demonstrations conducted in 2019 and 2024 by entities affiliated with our founder and by our technology partners. Our liquid energy solution encompasses biogas generation from tequila stillage (vinasse) through tropicalized anaerobic digestion processes, which can be utilized in on-site cogeneration (simultaneous thermal and electrical energy) or in a steam boiler. This process also yields two byproducts: treated water that is intended to meet Mexican discharge standards and digestate (biodigestion sludge) that holds value as a fertilizer in regenerative agriculture.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The anticipated revenue streams for solid waste encompass the direct sale of pellets to consumers or, alternatively, the sale of steam for their processing needs. We believe the pellets we intend to produce will provide a more cost-effective and environmentally sustainable alternative, with a &#8220;neutral&#8221; carbon footprint, to the fossil fuels most frequently utilized in the tequila industry today, including fuel oil, natural gas and LP gas. Projected revenue streams for liquid solutions derive primarily from the sale of purified biogas, which can be utilized in industrial processes as an alternative to fossil fuels, for transportation, or integrated directly into the electrical infrastructure. In addition, the biodigestion of tequila vinasse produces by-products that are appropriate for agricultural irrigation or for release into national water bodies, as well as a biodigestate that can be composted and utilized as a natural fertilizer. As an auxiliary revenue stream for both solutions, we intend to charge a fixed treatment fee billed directly to clients.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Sustainable energy production, such as that derived from biogas obtained through stillage cogeneration, may be supported by Clean Energy Certificates (&#8220;CELs&#8221;) under Mexico&#8217;s Energy Transition Law. A CEL represents the production of one megawatt-hour of clean electricity. CELs are transacted on the Wholesale Electricity Market (MEM) in Mexico through contractual agreements or market transactions, and their value is established by the availability of clean energy generators and </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>4</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>the demand from obligated participants (suppliers and significant consumers), who are required to meet a specified minimum percentage of clean energy usage. Non-compliance by obligated entities in the purchase of CELs is subject to penalties under the Electric Industry Law. Our business plan does not depend on CELs. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Business Model</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our business model commences with negotiations among tequila producers, waste generators and Biointra. In most instances, prospective clients are concerned with the proper disposal of their waste in compliance with Mexican laws and regulations. In Mexico, tequila bagasse and vinasse are classified as &#8220;special waste,&#8221; and legislation stipulates that responsibility for them lies with the generator, in accordance with the Integrated Waste Management Law of the State of Jalisco (LGIREJ) and its regulations concerning the collection and transportation of special waste. As an auxiliary negotiation instrument, we intend to offer renewable energy for the client&#8217;s production process at a competitive rate relative to conventional fossil fuels, along with a business model that enables equipment modernization with no capital investment by the client. Once the volume of waste warrants the establishment of a treatment facility, we intend to allocate resources toward fixed assets, including machinery, land and construction, to serve predominantly local clients. Following the commencement of operations, which we estimate would occur approximately 12 to 18 months after construction begins, depending on the supplier&#8217;s delivery schedule, we intend to charge a predetermined fixed treatment fee for both solid and liquid processing.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Solid processes are founded on a &#8220;tropicalized&#8221; methodology that encompasses pretreatment and processing of raw materials, along with pelletizing and cooling procedures, to transform raw waste into industrial-grade pellets suitable for the industry. For liquid processes, we would receive effluent in accordance with governmental standards for homogenization and subsequently subject it to both aerobic and anaerobic treatment to generate biogas. To adhere to Mexican regulations, the effluent would be subjected to ozone treatment to attain the water quality necessary for discharge into national water bodies or for use in agricultural irrigation. Our business model contemplates the receipt of residual materials at our facilities, with transportation costs borne by the client.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We intend to operate under an energy services company (&#8220;ESCO&#8221;) model with three contracting modalities: (1) energy supply contracts, (2) technical systems management, and (3) performance contracts. For thermal energy produced from agave pellets, our model incorporates the installation of specialized boilers designed for pellet combustion and steam generation. The capacity of the available furnaces accommodates the range of requirements of the tequila industry, with continuous production throughout the year. The furnaces utilize Spanish technology from the Termomass Am&#233;rica brand and are intended to be manufactured in Mexico to optimize cost efficiency.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our target customers are located primarily in five regions within the Mexican state of Jalisco: Tequila, Arandas, Atotonilco, Tepatitl&#225;n and Guadalajara. Management believes that, if the planned operating units in these five regions are financed and built, Biointra would have the capacity to serve a substantial portion of the tequila producers in those regions.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We depend on the technological support of our international collaborators to ensure compliance with local regulations. Our planned facilities require a limited workforce, with approximately three personnel per shift at a stillage facility and ten individuals involved in pellet production. Most of the production facilities are designed to be integrated into IoT systems to facilitate a continuous exchange of information among operations, suppliers and management.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>A key distinguishing factor of our solutions is their design for compliance with Mexican legislation and regulations concerning effluent discharges, including NOM-001-SEMARNAT-2021, which establishes the permissible limits for contaminants in wastewater discharges into receiving bodies owned by the nation and serves as the primary regulation concerning water quality standards for industrial water treatment. Our processes are also designed to meet international standards that support companies in achieving their decarbonization objectives. We believe our business model is increasingly competitive due to the rising cost of fossil fuels and the extensive availability and diversity of biomass in Mexico. Because our processes utilize waste materials, we expect our feedstock to be available at little or no cost.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Development Plan and Status</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We have not yet secured binding customer contracts for a specified volume of waste, and we have no operating treatment facility. Under management&#8217;s current development plan, construction of the first waste-to-energy operating units (the Tequila/Magdalena/Valles vinasse and pellet units) is scheduled to begin in January 2027, followed by the Atotonilco units in June 2027, in each case contingent upon obtaining the necessary project financing, land and environmental permits. As of the date of this Amendment, environmental permitting for the first region was approximately 50% complete and had not been </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>5</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>started for the other regions. Accordingly, we do not expect to generate revenue from waste-to-energy operations during 2026. See &#8220;Item 2. Financial Information &#8212;&nbsp;Outlook and Development Plan.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Acquisition of Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V.</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>On April 22, 2025, we entered into a Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA, a Mexican corporation controlled by our Chief Executive Officer. Pursuant to the agreement, on May 6, 2025 we issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock to Mr. Lahud to acquire 99 of the 100 outstanding shares of BRA (the remaining share being retained by Mr. Lahud as described under &#8220;Corporate Information&#8221; above). The transfer of BRA&#8217;s Series &#8220;I&#8221; Class &#8220;A&#8221; shares to the Company was formalized by Public Deed No. 33,148 dated July 30, 2025, granted before Notary Public No. 232 of Mexico City, which also amended BRA&#8217;s bylaws to permit the admission of foreign shareholders, and the definitive share certificates were delivered on August 4, 2025. The Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement closed upon the Company obtaining control of BRA on August 8, 2025. Pursuant to ASC 805-50-30-5, the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition under common control; the transfer of the net assets of BRA does not constitute a business and therefore does not represent a change in the reporting entity. At the closing, we recognized the net assets of BRA at their historical carrying value of $421, and the difference between the fair value of the shares issued and the net assets of BRA was recognized in additional paid-in capital. BRA is consolidated in our financial statements from August 8, 2025. See Note 3 to our audited consolidated financial statements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Acquisition of Agricultural Property by BRA (the &#8220;BRA Land Acquisition&#8221;)</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>On September 15, 2025, BRA entered into a Real Property Purchase Agreement (contribution-in-kind agreement) with Mr. Juan Pablo Mu&#241;oz Flores (the &#8220;Seller&#8221;), an unrelated third party, under which the Seller transferred to BRA four parcels of agricultural real property in the States of Jalisco and Nayarit, Mexico, together with the land improvements, buildings, irrigation and hydraulic infrastructure, water-use rights and avocado and blue agave plantations located on them, in exchange for 1,500,000 shares of our Class A Common Stock. The obligation to issue the shares was assigned to the Company under an Assignment of Assets against Share Issuance Agreement between BRA and the Company and a Three-Party Assignment of Land Purchase and Share Issuance Agreement among BRA, the Company and the Seller. For Mexican tax purposes the parties fixed the transfer value at MXN 95,765,000. The transfer of title was formalized by Public Deeds Nos. 1,755, 1,756 and 1,757, each dated December 28, 2025, and Public Deed No. 1,758, dated December 29, 2025, each granted before Notary Public No. 198 of Altamira, Tamaulipas. BRA obtained control of the properties upon execution of the agreement, and the properties are under active cultivation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We recorded the acquired assets at a fair value of $5,426,066 (MXN 99,652,094), determined from four third-party agricultural appraisal reports (using the cultivated-area valuation for each property) and observable market data. The fair value was allocated as follows: land $3,484,510; bearer plants (avocado) $285,749; inventory (blue agave) $1,375,868; land improvements $191,432; buildings $46,912; and water licenses (intangible assets) $41,595. The 1,500,000 shares were presented as shares issuable at December 31, 2025; their issuance was approved on January 10, 2026 and the shares were recorded in the register maintained by our transfer agent on February 22, 2026. On July 24, 2026, the Seller executed a sworn declaration, ratified before a notary public, confirming that all four parcels formed part of the transaction and that the 1,500,000 shares constitute the full consideration. The valuation of the acquired property was identified by our independent registered public accounting firm as a critical audit matter. See &#8220;Item 3. Properties&#8221; and Notes 4, 6, 7 and 8 to our audited consolidated financial statements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Agricultural Operations</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Through BRA, we own agricultural properties that include land, water rights, buildings, irrigation infrastructure and avocado and blue agave bearer plants. These properties are under active cultivation. The agricultural operations are intended to preserve and develop the productive value of the acquired properties and to provide operational flexibility, potential agricultural inputs and potential cash flows while we develop our waste-to-energy initiatives. The properties are also intended to serve as sites for the development of our waste-to-energy operations. As of the date of this Amendment, we have not recognized revenue from the sale of agricultural products.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Production and harvest cycles.</B> Our two principal crops have different production cycles. Avocado trees are perennial: once mature, a tree produces fruit that is harvested annually, generally over several months of each year, and the tree itself remains in place and continues to produce in subsequent seasons. Blue agave (<I>Agave tequilana</I> Weber, azul variety) is cultivated for its heart, or <I>pi&#241;a</I>, which is harvested once, when the plant reaches maturity, generally six to eight years after planting; harvesting the pi&#241;a removes the plant, which must then be replaced by new plantings. Accordingly, harvest does not consume our avocado trees but does consume each agave plant that is harvested.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>6</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Accounting presentation.</B> We account for our agricultural activities under ASC 905, Agriculture. The avocado trees acquired with the agricultural properties are presented within property and equipment as bearer plants and are depreciated over four years. The agave plantations acquired with the agricultural properties are presented as inventory and the cultivating costs that we establish in the future, will be accumulated as growing crops in inventory and charged to cost of sales when the products are sold, and when an acquired agave plantation is harvested its remaining carrying amount will be charged to cost of sales. See Note 2 to our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements as of June 30, 2026. We had no harvested crops, or agricultural products at June 30, 2026 or December 31, 2025, and we have not sold any agricultural products through the date of this Amendment.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Commercial Pipeline: Letters of Intent and Confidentiality Agreements</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Between January 2024 and July 2025, Biointra Renovables Tequila Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V., an entity affiliated with our Chief Executive Officer, and BRA executed four letters of intent (&#8220;LOIs&#8221;) with tequila and agave producers in the Tequila Denomination of Origin region, each of which remains in effect. The LOIs are non-binding. They record the parties&#8217; intention to explore the development of waste collection and transformation centers for bagasse and vinasse, impose mutual confidentiality obligations, and expressly state that they do not create any obligation to purchase or sell services, any partnership or joint venture, or any liability for damages. None of the LOIs specifies a price, a committed volume or a term of service. The LOIs were executed by the following entities:</P>
