<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 2. FINANCIAL INFORMATION</B></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>MANAGEMENT&#8217;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our audited consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, for the year ended December 31, 2025 and for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024, and our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements as of June 30, 2026 and for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and the related notes, which appear beginning on page F-1 of this Amendment. This discussion contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. See &#8220;Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements&#8221; and &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Overview</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Biointra is a development-stage company that is building an integrated platform for the recovery and beneficial use of organic waste from the tequila industry in Mexico, including the conversion of bagasse into biomass pellets and of vinasse into biogas. On August 8, 2025, we obtained control of our operating subsidiary, BRA, and on September 15, 2025, BRA acquired four agricultural properties in exchange for 1,500,000 shares of our Class A Common Stock. Our consolidated financial statements include the accounts of BRA from August 8, 2025. We have not generated revenue since inception, and our operations have been funded by advances from a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer and by non-cash issuances of our Class A Common Stock. Our expenses consist principally of consulting fees (most of which have been settled in shares), depreciation and amortization of the agricultural property and water licenses acquired by BRA, legal, audit and other professional fees, and transfer agent fees associated with our registration and planned listing.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Recent Developments</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On January 10, 2026, our board approved the issuance of 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock to Silver Rock as the commitment fee under the Share Purchase Agreement and of 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock to the Seller in the BRA Land Acquisition. Both blocks were recorded in the register maintained by our transfer agent on February 22, 2026, after which 123,611,456 shares of Class A Common Stock and 10,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock were outstanding.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On February 23, 2026, we filed a notice on Form D with the SEC with respect to our 2024 private placement, and on March 2, 2026, we filed the Original Filing.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>During the six months ended June 30, 2026, Mr. Lahud and a company he controls advanced an aggregate of $126,588 to us, including cash advances of $3,500 on February 19, 2026, $50,000 on March 10, 2026 and $30,000 on April 8, 2026, and expenses paid on our behalf. The advances are non-interest-bearing, unsecured and due on demand. &nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On June 26, 2026, we issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share to Mr. Lahud, as directed by the creditor, in settlement of $315,421 of advances owed to Lahud150, S.A. de C.V., a company controlled by Mr. Lahud, of which $5 was forgiven and treated as a capital contribution to the Company. The issuance was approved by unanimous written consent of our board of directors dated June 26, 2026, with Mr. Niembro, as the disinterested director, approving the transaction. The shares were issued and outstanding as of June 30, 2026.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>From February through April 2026, BRA&#8217;s former bank account was blocked and BRA operated without an active bank account until a new account was opened in May 2026. During that period BRA&#8217;s expenses were paid by affiliates of our Chief Executive Officer.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On July 24, 2026, the Seller in the BRA Land Acquisition executed a sworn declaration, ratified before a notary public, confirming the sale of all four parcels and his receipt of the 1,500,000 shares as full consideration.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On September 24, 2026, Productores Industriales de Biomasa, S.A. de C.V. executed the biomass supply agreement described under &#8220;Item 1. Business &#8212;&nbsp;Biomass Supply Arrangement,&#8221; which has not been countersigned by the Company and is not in effect.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On November 4, 2026, Fruci &amp; Associates II, PLLC issued its report on our consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, which includes an explanatory paragraph regarding substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern and a critical audit matter relating to the valuation of the acquired agricultural property. In connection with the audit, our auditor also communicated to our board a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting. See &#8220;Internal Control over Financial Reporting&#8221; below.&nbsp;</P>

<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Revenue.</B> We did not generate revenue in any of the periods presented. We have no operating waste-to-energy facility, and no sales of agricultural products were recorded through June 30, 2026.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Operating expenses.</B> Total operating expenses increased to $202,081 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $57,355 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, and to $488,302 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $59,125 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increases were principally attributable to the following:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Amortization and depreciation</B> of $33,204 and $66,075 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively (nil in 2025), consisting of depreciation of the bearer plants, land improvements and buildings acquired by BRA in September 2025 ($63,890 for the six months) and amortization of the water licenses ($2,185 for the six months). Bearer plants and land improvements are depreciated over four years and buildings over 20 years. Because the BRA Land Acquisition closed in September 2025, no comparable charge was recorded in the 2025 periods.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Consulting</B> expense of $100,000 and $279,000 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $50,000 in each 2025 period. The three-month and six-month 2026 amounts include $100,000 and $250,000, respectively, of non-cash expense representing the remaining amortization, through the end of the service period on May 31, 2026, of the $600,000 fair value of the 6,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issued to four consultants on May 6, 2025, and $29,000 of cash consulting fees. The 2025 amounts represent the initial amortization of that award.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Legal and professional fees</B> of $16,002 and $68,245 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $5,500 in each 2025 period, reflecting audit, accounting and legal fees associated with the audit of our 2025 financial statements, the Original Filing and this Amendment.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Transfer agent fees</B> of $24,235 and $45,705 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $1,450 and $2,549 in the 2025 periods, reflecting the fees charged by our transfer agent for the issuance of the Silver Rock and BRA Land Acquisition shares, certificate cancellations and legend removals, and monthly services.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>General and administrative</B> expenses of $28,640 and $29,277 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $306 and $581 in the 2025 periods, reflecting filing, bank and administrative costs of the Company and BRA.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Other expense.</B> We recorded interest expense of $22 in the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 on an overdue professional fee invoice. No other income or expense was recorded in the periods presented.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Net loss and comprehensive loss.</B> Net loss was $202,103 and $488,324 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $57,355 and $59,125 for the corresponding 2025 periods. We recorded foreign currency translation gains of $143,445 and $153,937 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, in other comprehensive income, arising from the translation of BRA&#8217;s peso-denominated net assets, principally the agricultural property, at the higher period-end exchange rate. Comprehensive loss was $58,658 and $334,387 for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, </P>

<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Revenue.</B> We generated no revenue in either period, as we remained in the development stage. During these periods we focused on project development, the acquisition of BRA and of the agricultural properties, and discussions with tequila producers and other industrial partners in Mexico. There were no costs of goods sold or gross profit in either period.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Operating expenses.</B> Operating expenses increased to $963,691 for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $39,560 for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to (i) consulting expense of $350,000, representing the portion recognized in 2025 of the $600,000 fair value of the 6,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issued on May 6, 2025 for services to be rendered from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 (the remaining $250,000 was recorded as a prepaid expense at December 31, 2025); (ii) depreciation of $30,344 and amortization of $1,038 on the agricultural property and water licenses acquired by BRA; (iii) legal and professional fees of $15,773 and transfer agent fees of $5,224 associated with our registration process; and (iv) loss on write-down of inventory to net realizable value of $559,798 on the unharvested agave plantations acquired by BRA. Consulting expense in 2024 consisted principally of fees paid to advisors in connection with our organization and the private placement.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Other expense.</B> We incurred no other expense in 2025. In the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024, we incurred a commitment fee of $217,866, representing the fair value of the 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock issuable to Silver Rock under the Share Purchase Agreement, and financing expense of $75,960, representing the portion of the $89,240 of costs of our 2024 private placement that exceeded the gross proceeds of the placement.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Net loss and comprehensive loss.</B> Net loss was $963,691 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $333,386 for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024. Of the 2025 net loss, $371,256 was incurred in the United States and $592,435 in Mexico. After a foreign currency translation gain of $95,430, comprehensive loss for 2025 was $868,261. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.01) for both Class A and Class B Common Stock for the year ended December 31, 2025 and $(0.00) for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024, based on weighted average shares outstanding of 116,135,540 Class A shares and 10,000,000 Class B shares for the year ended December 31, 2025, and 90,021,924 Class A shares and 8,270,042 Class B shares for the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>As of June 30, 2026, we had cash of $15,602 and a working capital of $864,087, compared to cash of $33,931 and working capital of $945,015 at December 31, 2025. The change in working capital principally reflects the amortization of the $250,000 prepaid consulting expense, an increase of $51,167 in accounts payable and accrued liabilities (principally audit, legal and transfer agent fees) and a decrease of $188,833 in amounts due to a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer. Current assets at June 30, 2026 include deferred financing costs of $120,000, which relate to our planned registration statement on Form S-1 and are not available to fund operations. Total stockholders&#8217; equity decreased to $5,025,239 at June 30, 2026 from $5,044,205 at December 31, 2025, reflecting the net loss for the period, partially offset by the foreign currency translation gain and by the $315,421 of related-party debt settled through the issuance of shares on June 26, 2026. The issuance in the first quarter of 2026 of the 3,678,656 shares that were presented as issuable at December 31, 2025 reclassified $5,643,932 from shares issuable to common stock and additional paid-in capital and had no effect on total equity.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>At December 31, 2025, we had cash of $33,931 and working capital of $945,015, compared to cash of $9,989 and a working capital deficit of $115,401 at December 31, 2024. Current assets at December 31, 2025 included prepaid consulting expenses of $250,000, deferred financing costs of $110,000, and inventory of $831,142 that were not available to fund operations. Total stockholders&#8217; equity increased to $5,044,205 at December 31, 2025, principally as a result of the 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issuable for the agricultural property ($5,426,066) and the shares issued for services ($600,000), partially offset by the net loss for the year.</P>

Financing activities consisted of $10,000 of deferred financing costs. Net cash used in operating activities in the six months ended June 30, 2025 was $10,076, as the net loss of $59,125 was substantially offset by non-cash stock-based consulting expense of $50,000 and by advances from a related party of $30,024, partially offset by a decrease in accounts payable and accrued liabilities of $30,975; the balance was funded by a bank overdraft of $87.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Year ended December 31, 2025.</B> Net cash provided by operating activities of $87,425 reflected advances of $123,884 from a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer, which funded the net loss after non-cash charges for stock-based compensation ($350,000), depreciation and amortization ($31,382) and loss on write-down of inventory to net realizable value ($559,798). Investing activities consisted of $89 of cash acquired with BRA. Financing activities consisted of $65,000 of deferred financing costs, partially offset by $800 of proceeds from the issuance of Class A Common Stock and $580 of net subscription proceeds.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We anticipate that cash flows from operations will remain negative until revenue-generating operations commence following the commissioning of our first waste-to-energy facility, which under our current development plan would not occur before 2028.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Related-Party Advances</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>Since inception, we have obtained undocumented, unsecured, non-interest-bearing, due-on-demand advances from a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer, and from Mr. Lahud personally, to fund our operations, and that company has paid deferred financing costs, prepaid consulting fees and general and administrative expenses on our behalf. The balance owed was $35,441 at June 30, 2026, $224,274 at December 31, 2025 and $100,390 at December 31, 2024. These advances are not committed, and Mr. Lahud and his affiliates may discontinue them at any time. On June 26, 2026, we issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock to Mr. Lahud in settlement of $315,421 of advances due to Lahud150, S.A. de C.V., a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer, of which $5 was forgiven and treated as a contribution to the Company. &nbsp;See &#8220;Item 7. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence.&#8221;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Going Concern</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our financial statements have been prepared on a going-concern basis, which assumes that we will be able to meet our obligations and continue our operations for at least one year from the date the financial statements are issued. We have not achieved profitable operations, expect to incur further losses in the development of our business, had an accumulated deficit of $1,785,401 at June 30, 2026 and do not have sufficient cash to meet our obligations. These factors raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern, and our auditor&#8217;s report on our 2025 financial statements includes an explanatory paragraph to that effect. Our ability to continue as a going concern depends on our ability to obtain equity financing, project financing and continued related-party advances. Management has no formal plan in place to address this condition other than its intention to raise equity capital following our planned listing, including under the Silver Rock Share Purchase Agreement, and to continue to rely on related-party advances in the interim. There is no assurance that additional funding will be available. See Note 13 to our audited consolidated financial statements and Note 12 to our unaudited interim financial statements.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Material Cash Requirements and Plan of Operation for the Next Twelve Months</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>During the next twelve months we expect our cash requirements to consist of (i) the legal, accounting, audit, transfer agent, listing and filing costs of completing this registration, our planned Nasdaq listing and our planned registration statement on Form S-1, which we estimate at approximately $400,000 to $600,000; (ii) the cost of maintaining the BRA properties under cultivation and of the water concession; (iii) the environmental permitting and engineering work required before construction of our first operating units can begin; and (iv) general corporate expenses. We will also need to begin raising the project financing for the first operating units if construction is to begin in 2027 as planned. We intend to meet these requirements through a combination of proceeds from the sale of our Class A Common Stock in private placements and, following a listing, under the Silver Rock Share Purchase Agreement, other equity, debt and project financing arrangements, and related-party advances from our Chief Executive Officer and entities he controls, which are not committed. We have no committed sources of financing. Failure to obtain sufficient financing would materially and adversely affect our ability to execute our business plan.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Future financing is expected to be directed toward the construction and commissioning of waste-to-energy facilities, the acquisition of specialized equipment and technology, the expansion of feedstock supply agreements and working capital to support regulatory compliance, staffing and project development. We may use short-term loans, long-term debt, equity capital </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>23</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>and project financing as may be necessary, but there can be no assurance that such financing will be available on commercially reasonable terms, if at all.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Outlook and Development Plan</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The following information is forward-looking, has been prepared by management, and has not been examined, compiled or reviewed by our independent registered public accounting firm, which expresses no opinion or any other form of assurance on it. It is presented in reliance on Item 10(b) of Regulation S-K, and investors should not place undue reliance on it.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Based on the letters of intent described under &#8220;Item 1. Business &#8212;&nbsp;Commercial Pipeline,&#8221; management projects <B>no revenue from waste-to-energy operations for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026</B>. The principal assumptions are the following: (i) none of the LOIs is a binding contract or contains price or volume commitments; (ii) we have no operating treatment plant, and under management&#8217;s development plan construction of the first operating units (the Tequila/Magdalena/Valles vinasse and pellet units) is scheduled to begin in January 2027, followed by the Atotonilco units in June 2027; and (iii) as of the date of this Amendment, environmental permits for the first region were approximately 50% complete and had not been started for the other regions. We likewise project no material revenue from the sale of agricultural products in 2026, because no such sales were recorded through June 30, 2026.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>For reference, the counterparties to the three LOIs that include waste-generation data reported annualized volumes of approximately 32,800 cubic meters of vinasse and 4,100 metric tons of bagasse. This is about 15% of the approximately 219,000 cubic meters of annual design capacity of the first planned vinasse unit (600 cubic meters per day). For illustration only, if all of the reported vinasse volume were contracted at the treatment fee assumed in management&#8217;s financial model (US$18.15 per cubic meter), annual vinasse treatment-fee revenue would be approximately US$0.6 million. No such contracts exist, and this amount is not a forecast for 2026 or any other period. Management&#8217;s integrated financial model for its planned operating units is under revision, and we are not presenting projections from that model.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Modeled capital expenditures are the amounts used in management&#8217;s financial model and are stated at an exchange rate of MXN 18.50 per U.S. dollar, based on supplier quotations, some of which require updating. Validated capital expenditures reflect management&#8217;s subsequent unit-by-unit review of those quotations and total approximately $55.3 million, compared to approximately $62.3 million in the financial model; the difference principally reflects lower validated costs for the pellet units and the Arandas vinasse unit, partially offset by a higher validated cost for the Zapopan/Guadalajara vinasse unit. <P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>As of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, we had no off-balance sheet arrangements, as defined in Item 303(b)(1)(ii)(B) of Regulation S-K. Our use, at no charge, of office premises and administrative support provided by entities affiliated with our Chief Executive Officer is not an off-balance sheet arrangement and is described under &#8220;Item 7. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence.&#8221; Our obligations under the Silver Rock Share Purchase Agreement, </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>24</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>including the obligation to issue warrants upon a public listing, are described in Note 14 to our audited consolidated financial statements and Note 13 to our unaudited interim financial statements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Internal Control over Financial Reporting</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>In connection with the audit of our consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, our independent registered public accounting firm communicated to our board of directors that there are not effective policies and procedures in place to provide adequate, independent oversight over financial reporting, timely preparation, review and approval of accounting records, and preparation and entry of journal entries, and that there is a lack of segregation of duties, and that these deficiencies constitute a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting. We have engaged an outside accounting firm to maintain our books and prepare our consolidated financial statements, and management is evaluating further improvements, including the recruitment of independent directors to form an audit committee and the adoption of written closing and review procedures. The material weakness had not been remediated as of June 30, 2026 or as of the date of this Amendment. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our significant accounting policies are described in Note 2 to our audited consolidated financial statements. We base our estimates on historical experience and on assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, and actual results may differ. The estimates we consider most critical are the following:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Fair value and allocation of the acquired agricultural property.</B> The fair value of $5,426,066 assigned to the BRA Land Acquisition was determined from third-party appraisals using market comparables for land, replacement cost for land improvements and buildings, crop establishment and maintenance costs referenced to data of Fideicomisos Instituidos en Relaci&#243;n con la Agricultura (FIRA) for bearer plants, and water-right valuation inputs for the water concession, and was allocated among land, bearer plants, land improvements, buildings and water licenses on the basis of those appraisals. The appraisals involve significant judgment, and the valuation was identified by our auditor as a critical audit matter.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Useful lives.</B> Bearer plants and land improvements are depreciated on a straight-line basis over four years, buildings over 20 years, and water licenses over the ten-year term of the concession. A change in these lives would change our depreciation and amortization expense, which was $66,075 for the six months ended June 30, 2026.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Impairment of long-lived assets.</B> We review property and equipment and intangible assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable, by comparing the carrying amount of the asset group to the undiscounted cash flows expected from its use and eventual disposition. No impairment was recognized in the periods presented.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Fair value of shares issued for services and other non-cash consideration.</B> Because there is no public market for our shares, the fair value of shares issued for services, as a commitment fee and as consideration for assets is determined by reference to the price of contemporaneous cash sales, the fair value of the assets or services received, or other available evidence, and is recognized over the requisite service period where applicable.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Income taxes.</B> We record a full valuation allowance against our deferred tax assets because we cannot conclude that it is more likely than not that they will be realized.&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>See Note 2 to our audited consolidated financial statements and Note 2 to our unaudited interim financial statements for a discussion of recently issued accounting pronouncements and their expected effect on our financial statements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>As a smaller reporting company, we are not required to provide the information called for by Item 305 of Regulation S-K. Our principal market risk is foreign currency risk arising from the Mexican peso functional currency of BRA, as described under &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 3. PROPERTIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Through our subsidiary BRA, we own four parcels of agricultural real property in Mexico acquired in the BRA Land Acquisition and recorded at an acquisition-date fair value of <B>US$5,426,066</B> (MXN 99,652,094). The properties are under active cultivation with avocado and blue agave and are also intended to serve as sites for the development of our waste-to-energy operations, including biomass pelletization and biogas production facilities. <P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Each deed was granted before Notary Public No. 198 of Altamira, Tamaulipas. The &#8220;Las Lomas&#8221; property is a fraction of the tract described in Public Instrument No. 4,755 granted before Notary Public No. 2 of Tequila, Jalisco, and is planted with blue agave registered with the Tequila Regulatory Council (Consejo Regulador del Tequila). The acquired assets also include water-use rights under a concession covering 60,000 cubic meters per year, which were transferred to BRA by a Water Concession Transfer Agreement with the Seller and are recorded as an intangible asset with a carrying amount of $40,472 at June 30, 2026 ($41,367 at December 31, 2025). The acquisition-date fair value of the acquired property was allocated to land ($3,484,510), bearer plants ($285,749), inventory ($1,375,868), land improvements ($191,432), buildings ($46,912) and water licenses ($41,595). At June 30, 2026, the carrying amount of property and equipment was $4,120,680, net of accumulated depreciation of $95,966, after translation of BRA&#8217;s peso-denominated balances at the period-end exchange rate. The properties are not subject to any mortgage or other encumbrance. BRA is in the process of completing the registration of the deeds with the applicable Public Property Registries and of the water concession transfer with CONAGUA.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We do not own or lease any other real property. Our principal executive office at 1041 N. Dupont Hwy #1029, Dover, Delaware 19901 is a registered office address that serves as our legal and administrative headquarters for incorporation and compliance purposes. Our officers work from premises in Mexico made available by entities affiliated with our Chief Executive Officer at no cost to the Company. There is no written lease or other agreement for these premises, no rent or other charge has been paid or accrued, and our financial statements do not include any expense for their use. Management estimates that the fair rental value of the office space used by the Company is not material to our results of operations. See &#8220;Item 7. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence.&#8221; We believe these arrangements are adequate for our current needs.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 4. SECURITY OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN BENEFICIAL OWNERS AND MANAGEMENT</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The following table sets forth, as of November 4, 2026, information regarding the beneficial ownership of our Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock by (i) each person known to us to be the beneficial owner of more than 5% of either class, (ii) each of our directors and executive officers, and (iii) all of our directors and executive officers as a group. Beneficial ownership is determined in accordance with Rule 13d-3 under the Exchange Act, which provides that a beneficial owner includes any person who directly or indirectly has or shares voting power or investment power with respect to a security, or who has the right to acquire beneficial ownership of the security within 60 days, including through the exercise of any option, warrant or conversion right. Shares subject to such rights are deemed outstanding for the purpose of computing the percentage ownership of the person holding them but not for the purpose of computing the percentage ownership of any other person. Except as otherwise indicated, the persons named in the table have sole voting and investment power with respect to all shares shown, subject to community property laws where applicable. Unless otherwise indicated, the address of each beneficial owner is c/o Biointra, Corp., 1041 N. Dupont Hwy #1029, Dover, Delaware 19901.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Percentages of class are based on 123,650,883 shares of Class A Common Stock and 10,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock outstanding as of November 4, 2026. Each share of Class A Common Stock is entitled to one vote and each share of Class B Common Stock is entitled to twenty votes; the percentage of total voting power is based on 323,650,883 total votes.</P>

<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz</B>, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. Mr. Lahud is a Mexican businessman with over four decades of multi-sector experience in the textile, construction and renewable energy (biomass) industries. He has promoted biomass projects for clean energy generation and, through LAHUD150, S.A. de C.V. and Biointra Renovables Tequila Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V., entities he controls, developed the relationships with tequila producers and technology partners on which our business plan is based. He founded the Company in 2024. We believe Mr. Lahud&#8217;s experience in the Mexican industrial sector and his role as our founder qualify him to serve as a director.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Mart&#237;n Niembro Fragoso</B>, Director and Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Niembro has over 40 years of experience (1980&#8211;2023) leading administration, finance and general management functions. He specializes in corporate and real estate finance, auditing, financial modeling, the design of business models and the structuring of sustainable real estate projects, and has served as an independent board member of companies in the construction, communications and entertainment industries. We believe Mr. Niembro&#8217;s financial management and governance experience qualify him to serve as a director.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Ra&#250;l Seiji Lahud Hirasawa, Director. Mr. Lahud Hirasawa, age 27, has served as a director since [&#9679;]. Since 2026 he has served as Senior Coordinator of New Projects of Biointra Group, in which role he coordinates the Company&#8217;s proposed direct listing on Nasdaq, including the legal and financial compliance workstreams, and manages the vendor relationships supporting the expansion of the Company&#8217;s production capacity. From 2023 to 2025 he served as Coordinator of New Projects of Biointra Group, where he managed the planning and execution of the Company&#8217;s waste-</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>27</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>to-energy facility in Jalisco, Mexico, and negotiated long-term agreements with vendors. He joined Biointra Group in 2021 as a General Intern and held that position until his appointment as Coordinator of New Projects in 2023. Mr. Lahud Hirasawa holds a Bachelor of Global Business degree from Tecnol&#243;gico de Monterrey, with a specialization in technological tools for the improvement of supply chains. Mr. Lahud Hirasawa is the son of Mr. Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz, our Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. We believe Mr. Lahud Hirasawa&#8217;s knowledge of our projects, vendors and listing process qualifies him to serve as a director.</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Juan Jos&#233; Michelena Alonso</B>, Director of Marketing. Mr. Michelena holds a master&#8217;s degree in financial risk and has led finance departments in organizations including ANUIES (the National Association of Universities and Higher Education Institutions of Mexico) and commercial banks. He directed operations at SEED Group and led sales as the Major League Baseball representative in Mexico, and specializes in risk mitigation, process development and regulatory compliance, with technical expertise in financial products, trusts and commercial law. Mr. Michelena is an executive officer and is not a member of our board of directors.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Family Relationships</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Mr. Ra&#250;l Seiji Lahud Hirasawa, a director, is the son of Mr. Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz, our Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. There are no other family relationships among our directors and executive officers.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Involvement in Certain Legal Proceedings</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>During the past ten years, none of our directors or executive officers has been involved in any legal proceeding of the type described in Item 401(f) of Regulation S-K, including any bankruptcy petition, criminal conviction or pending criminal proceeding, order or judgment barring or limiting involvement in any type of business, securities or banking activity, or finding of a violation of federal or state securities or commodities laws.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Board Composition, Committees and Director Independence</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our board of directors consists of three members, Mr. Lahud, Mr. Niembro and Mr. Lahud Hirasawa, none of whom is independent under the listing rules of Nasdaq. We do not have standing audit, compensation or nominating committees; the entire board performs those functions. We do not have an audit committee financial expert. Before our Class A Common Stock can be listed on Nasdaq we will be required to appoint independent directors and to establish an audit committee that satisfies Rule 10A-3 under the Exchange Act and the Nasdaq listing rules. Because Mr. Lahud controls more than 50% of our voting power, we will be a &#8220;controlled company&#8221; under the Nasdaq rules and may elect to rely on exemptions from the requirements to have a majority-independent board and independent compensation and nominating committees. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Code of Ethics</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We have not yet adopted a code of ethics applicable to our principal executive officer, principal financial officer and principal accounting officer. We intend to adopt a code of ethics and the other governance policies required by Nasdaq in connection with our planned listing.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Conflicts of Interest</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our directors and officers are, or may become, in their individual capacities, officers, directors, controlling stockholders or partners of other entities engaged in a variety of businesses, including LAHUD150, S.A. de C.V. and Biointra Renovables Tequila Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V. Potential conflicts of interest therefore exist, including with respect to time, effort and corporate opportunities. Our officers devote to our business such time as they believe to be necessary. Our Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws and board minutes contain no requirement that officers and directors disclose to us business opportunities that come to their attention; our officers and directors do, however, have a fiduciary duty of loyalty to the Company under Delaware law. We have no present intention of acquiring any business or business opportunity from any affiliate.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'>(1) Represents the par value of 100,000,000 founder shares of Class A Common Stock issued to Mr. Lahud upon our organization at $0.000001 per share. The 10,000,000 founder shares of Class B Common Stock issued to Mr. Lahud at the same time ($10) are not compensatory. The 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issued to Mr. Lahud on May 6, 2025 were consideration for the acquisition of BRA and are not compensation. See &#8220;Item 7. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Narrative Disclosure</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We have no employment agreements, consulting agreements or other arrangements with any of our executive officers, and we have no equity incentive plan, bonus plan, pension plan, deferred compensation arrangement or severance or change-in-control arrangement. There were no new compensation arrangements with, and no changes in the compensation of, our executive officers or directors during 2026 through the date of this Amendment. No stock options, restricted stock or other equity awards were outstanding at December 31, 2025 or at the date of this Amendment, and accordingly no table of outstanding equity awards at fiscal year-end is presented. We expect to adopt an equity incentive plan and to enter into employment arrangements with our executive officers in connection with or following our planned listing.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Director Compensation</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our directors received no compensation for their service as directors in 2025 or 2024. We have not adopted a director compensation policy. We expect to compensate independent directors, if and when appointed, with cash retainers and equity awards and to obtain directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 7. CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS, AND DIRECTOR INDEPENDENCE</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz, holds approximately 94.2% of the combined voting power of our common stock as of the date of this Amendment and therefore controls any stockholder vote. Since our inception, we have engaged in the following transactions with related persons, each of which involved an amount in excess of the lesser of $120,000 or 1% of the average of our total assets at year-end for the last two completed fiscal years, or which we otherwise consider material:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Founder shares.</B> In 2024, we issued 100,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock and 10,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock to Mr. Lahud as founder shares at par value, for aggregate consideration of $110.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Acquisition of BRA.</B> On April 22, 2025, we entered into a Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA, a Mexican corporation controlled by Mr. Lahud, and on May 6, 2025 we issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock to Mr. Lahud as consideration for 99 of the 100 outstanding shares of BRA. The transaction closed on August 8, 2025 and was accounted for as an asset acquisition under common control, with BRA&#8217;s net assets recognized at their historical carrying value of $421. Mr. Lahud retains one share of BRA. The terms of the transaction were determined by Mr. Lahud, as the controlling stockholder of both parties, and were not negotiated at arm&#8217;s length or approved by independent directors.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Advances and expenses paid on our behalf.</B> A company controlled by Mr. Lahud, and Mr. Lahud personally, have made cash advances to us and paid deferred financing costs, prepaid consulting fees and general and administrative &nbsp;</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>29</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'>expenses on our behalf. The balance owed was $35,441 at June 30, 2026, $224,274 at December 31, 2025 and $100,390 at December 31, 2024. Advances during the six months ended June 30, 2026 totaled $126,588, including cash advances of $3,500 on February 19, 2026, $50,000 on March 10, 2026 and $30,000 on April 8, 2026, and during the year ended December 31, 2025 totaled $123,884. On June 26, 2026, we issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share to Mr. Lahud, as directed by the creditor, in settlement of $315,421 of advances due to Lahud150, S.A. de C.V., a company controlled by Mr. Lahud, pursuant to a unanimous written consent of our board of directors of that date approved by Mr. Niembro as our disinterested director, of which $5 was forgiven and treated as a capital contribution to the Company. The largest aggregate amount outstanding since inception was $350,862, immediately before the June 26, 2026 settlement. These amounts are non-interest-bearing, unsecured and due on demand, and no amounts have been repaid in cash. The advances are not evidenced by a written agreement.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Use of affiliate premises and personnel.</B> Entities affiliated with Mr. Lahud provide office premises in Mexico and administrative support to the Company and BRA at no charge. During February through April 2026, when BRA had no active bank account, BRA&#8217;s expenses were paid by those affiliates and recorded as amounts due to related party. No rent, fee or other charge has been paid or accrued for these premises or services, there is no written agreement governing them, and no expense for them is reflected in our financial statements; management estimates that their fair value is not material to our results of operations. The affiliates may discontinue these arrangements at any time.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Affiliate letters of intent.</B> Three of the four letters of intent described under &#8220;Item 1. Business &#8212;&nbsp;Commercial Pipeline&#8221; were executed by Biointra Renovables Tequila Jalisco, S.A.P.I. de C.V., an entity controlled by Mr. Lahud that is not our subsidiary. These LOIs have not been assigned to the Company or BRA, and no consideration has been paid or is payable by the Company in respect of them. Any commercial contract arising from these relationships would need to be entered into by the Company or BRA, or assigned to it.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Policy for approval of related-party transactions.</B> We do not currently have a written policy for the review and approval of related-party transactions. Related-party transactions have been approved by our board of directors, both of whose members are interested in most of the transactions described above. We intend to adopt a written related-party transaction policy, administered by an independent audit committee, in connection with our planned Nasdaq listing.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Director independence.</B> Our board of directors has determined that neither of our directors is independent under Rule 5605(a)(2) of the Nasdaq listing rules or under Rule 10A-3 under the Exchange Act, because each is an executive officer of the Company. We have no independent directors and no committees of the board.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 8. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We are not a party to any pending legal proceeding, and to our knowledge no legal proceeding is threatened against us or against BRA, and no property of the Company or BRA is the subject of any pending legal proceeding. None of our officers, directors or holders of more than five percent of our common stock is a party to any legal proceeding adverse to us or has a material interest adverse to us.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 9. MARKET PRICE OF AND DIVIDENDS ON THE REGISTRANT&#8217;S COMMON EQUITY AND RELATED STOCKHOLDER MATTERS</B></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Market Information</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>There is no established public trading market for our Class A Common Stock or our Class B Common Stock, and our shares are not listed or quoted on any exchange or quotation system. On March 6, 2026, we submitted an application through the Nasdaq Listing Center to list our Class A Common Stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the proposed trading symbol &#8220;BCRP.&#8221; The application is pending and Nasdaq has not approved it. Based on our current stockholder base and financial condition, we do not yet satisfy Nasdaq&#8217;s initial listing requirements. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors &#8212;&nbsp;Risks Related to Our Securities.&#8221; The registration of our Class A Common Stock under Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act will become effective only upon Nasdaq&#8217;s certification of our listing. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors &#8212;&nbsp;Risks Related to Our Securities.&#8221;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Since inception, we have sold Class A Common Stock in private transactions at $0.10 per share (2024 and 2025) and have received subscriptions for 100 shares at $8.00 per share (2025). The 1,500,000 shares issued in the BRA Land Acquisition were recorded at a fair value of approximately $3.62 per share, and the 6,000,000 shares issued to consultants in May 2025 at $0.10 per share. The prices of our common equity in private transactions do not necessarily reflect the market price that may develop if and when our shares are listed on Nasdaq.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>30</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Holders of Record</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>As of November 4, 2026, based on the certified stockholder list of our transfer agent as of November 2, 2026, there were 306 holders of record of our Class A Common Stock and one holder of record of our Class B Common Stock. In some instances, a holder of record may be a broker or other entity holding shares in street name for one or more customers who beneficially own the shares.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Shares Eligible for Future Sale</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Rule 144 opinion of counsel.</B> On April 17, 2026, Oren Litwin LLC, our securities counsel, delivered to our transfer agent, Vstock Transfer, LLC, a blanket legal opinion under Rule 144 of the Securities Act (the &#8220;Rule 144 Opinion&#8221;), which is filed as Exhibit 99.3 to this Amendment. The Rule 144 Opinion covers the 123,611,456 shares of Class A Common Stock that were outstanding on the date of the opinion, held by 306 holders of record according to the transfer agent&#8217;s certified stockholder list as of April 1, 2026, and divides them into four groups: (i) 108,925,600 shares issued in 2024 and held by 288 holders (the &#8220;Early Shares&#8221;); (ii) 11,000,000 shares issued on May 6, 2025 to five holders, consisting of the 6,000,000 shares issued to four consultants and the 5,000,000 shares issued to Mr. Lahud in the BRA share exchange (the &#8220;Middle Shares&#8221;); (iii) the shares issued between November 13, 2025 and December 2, 2025 in our Regulation S offering (the &#8220;Recent Shares&#8221;); and (iv) the 1,500,000 shares issued to Mr. Mu&#241;oz Flores on February 22, 2026 in the BRA Land Acquisition (the &#8220;Flores Shares&#8221;). The 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock issued to Mr. Lahud on June 26, 2026 (see &#8220;Item 10. Recent Sales of Unregistered Securities&#8221;) were issued after the date of the Rule 144 Opinion and are not covered by it. Counsel concluded that the Company is not and has never been a &#8220;shell company&#8221; within the meaning of Rule 144(i), so that Rule 144 is available to our stockholders; that the Early Shares, having been held for more than one year, are no longer restricted; that the Middle Shares ceased to be restricted on May 6, 2026, one year after their issuance; and that the Recent Shares and the Flores Shares would cease to be restricted on July 30, 2026 and August 22, 2026, respectively, on the assumption that the Company would become subject to the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act sixty days after the filing of the Original Filing, so that the six-month holding period of Rule 144(d)(1)(i) would apply. Each holder relying on the Rule 144 Opinion must first deliver to us and to the transfer agent a representation letter stating, under penalty of perjury, whether the holder is an underwriter or an affiliate of the Company. The Rule 144 Opinion was delivered before the Original Filing was amended to reflect that our registration under Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act becomes effective only upon Nasdaq&#8217;s certification of our listing and not automatically sixty days after filing (see &#8220;Explanatory Note&#8221;). Because we are not yet subject to Exchange Act reporting, the one-year holding period of Rule 144(d)(1)(ii) continues to apply to the Recent Shares and the Flores Shares, and the dates stated in the Rule 144 Opinion for those two groups should be read accordingly; the Rule 144 Opinion&#8217;s conclusions as to shell-company status, the Early Shares and the Middle Shares are unaffected.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Unrestricted shares.</B> In reliance on the Rule 144 Opinion and the representation letters delivered by the holders, on May 11, 2026 our transfer agent removed the Securities Act restrictive legends from 14,924,800 shares of Class A Common Stock held by 287 holders of record who are not our affiliates, consisting of the Early Shares other than those held by Mr. Lahud and the 6,000,000 Middle Shares held by the four consultants. According to the transfer agent&#8217;s certified stockholder list as of November 2, 2026, these 14,924,800 shares are not restricted securities, are held in book-entry form without legend and may be sold without registration under Rule 144 or Section 4(a)(1) of the Securities Act at any time. Each of the 287 holders holds at least 400 shares, a &#8220;round lot&#8221; of 100 shares or more for purposes of the Nasdaq listing rules.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Shares that remain restricted or are held by an affiliate.</B> The remaining 108,726,083 shares of Class A Common Stock, as of November 4, 2026, consist of: (i) 105,039,427 shares held by Mr. Lahud, our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, comprising 100,000,000 Early Shares, the 5,000,000 Middle Shares and the 39,427 shares issued on June 26, 2026, which will have been held for one year on June 26, 2027; the Early Shares and the Middle Shares have been held for more than one year, but because Mr. Lahud is an affiliate all of his shares may be sold only in compliance with the volume, manner-of-sale, notice and current public information conditions of Rule 144 or pursuant to a registration statement; (ii) 8,000 Recent Shares held by seventeen holders of record, which will have been held for one year between November 13, 2026 and December 2, 2026 and will then be eligible for resale by those holders without restriction under Rule 144(b)(1)(i), or earlier if we have been subject to Exchange Act reporting for 90 days and are current in our reporting; (iii) the 1,500,000 Flores Shares, which will have been held for one year on February 22, 2027; and (iv) 2,178,656 shares issued to Silver Rock Group on February 22, 2026 as the commitment fee under the Share Purchase Agreement, which are not covered by the Rule 144 Opinion and will have been held for one year on February 22, 2027. All 10,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock are held by Mr. Lahud and are not convertible into Class A Common Stock.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>31</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Holders of unrestricted shares.</B> Upon the expiration of the one-year holding period for the Recent Shares in November and December 2026, 304 of our 306 holders of record as of November 4, 2026 &#8212;&nbsp;all of our holders of record other than Mr. Lahud and Silver Rock Group (Mr. Mu&#241;oz Flores holds 400 unrestricted shares in addition to the 1,500,000 Flores Shares) &#8212;&nbsp;will hold Class A Common Stock that is free of restrictions on resale, each in an amount of 400 shares or more. We therefore expect to have more than 300 round-lot holders of unrestricted shares for purposes of Nasdaq Listing Rule 5505(a)(3) by December 2026, although, as described under &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors,&#8221; we do not currently satisfy the requirement that at least half of those holders each hold unrestricted shares with a market value of at least $2,500, or the other quantitative initial listing requirements of the Nasdaq Capital Market.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Rule 144 generally.</B> Restricted securities may be sold in the public market only pursuant to an effective registration statement under the Securities Act or an exemption from registration, including Rule 144. In general, under Rule 144 as currently in effect, a person who is not our affiliate and has not been our affiliate during the preceding three months, and who has beneficially owned restricted securities for at least one year, may sell those securities without restriction. Once we have been subject to the reporting requirements of Section 13 or 15(d) of the Exchange Act for at least 90 days and are current in our reporting, the holding period for such a person is reduced to six months, and affiliates who have held restricted securities for at least six months may sell within any three-month period a number of shares that does not exceed the greater of 1% of the then-outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock (approximately 1,236,509 shares as of November 4, 2026) or the average weekly trading volume on Nasdaq during the four calendar weeks preceding the filing of a notice on Form 144, subject to manner-of-sale, notice and current public information requirements. Rule 144 is not available for the resale of securities of an issuer that is or was a shell company unless the conditions of Rule 144(i) are satisfied; as stated in the Rule 144 Opinion, we are not and have never been a shell company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Planned registration of Silver Rock shares.</B> In connection with our planned listing, we intend to file a registration statement on Form S-1 covering the resale by Silver Rock Group of the 2,178,656 commitment shares it holds and of the shares of Class A Common Stock that we may sell to Silver Rock Group under the Share Purchase Agreement following our listing. Under Amendment No. 1 to the Share Purchase Agreement dated November 2, 2026, the number of shares registered for resale by Silver Rock under any single registration statement may not exceed 29.99% of our then-outstanding shares, and no shares may be issued to Silver Rock under the agreement and the warrants (including the commitment shares) in excess of 19.99% of our shares outstanding immediately prior to our listing unless stockholder approval is obtained. No shares of our common stock are subject to outstanding options or warrants; upon a public listing we will be required to issue to Silver Rock warrants to purchase a number of shares of Class A Common Stock equal to 4% of our fully diluted outstanding shares. None of our stockholders has entered into a lock-up agreement.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Dividends</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We have never declared or paid cash dividends on our common stock and do not anticipate paying cash dividends in the foreseeable future. Any future determination to pay dividends will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend upon our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, the restrictions of applicable law, including the Delaware General Corporation Law, and other factors the board deems relevant. BRA&#8217;s ability to distribute funds to us is subject to Mexican corporate law, which requires the allocation of a portion of annual net profits to a legal reserve, and to Mexican withholding tax.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Securities Authorized for Issuance under Equity Compensation Plans</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>We have no equity compensation plans, and no securities are authorized for issuance under any such plan.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 10. RECENT SALES OF UNREGISTERED SECURITIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>During the past three years, we issued the following securities without registration under the Securities Act. Unless otherwise noted, the issuances were exempt from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and Rule 506(b) of Regulation D, as transactions by an issuer not involving a public offering, or under Regulation S, as offshore transactions with non-U.S. persons. No underwriter or placement agent was engaged in connection with any of these transactions, and no underwriting discounts or commissions were paid. In connection with the 2024 private placement of 132,800 shares of Class A Common Stock, we incurred $89,240 of offering costs, of which $13,280 was charged against the proceeds of the placement and $75,960 was recorded as financing expense. The deferred financing costs presented in our balance sheets ($120,000 at June 30, 2026) are costs directly related to our planned registered offering and listing and do not relate to any of the transactions described in </P>
