The shares issued in these transactions bore Securities Act restrictive legends when issued; see &#8220;Item 9 &#8212;&nbsp;Shares Eligible for Future Sale&#8221; for the shares from which the legends were subsequently removed.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>In 2024, we issued 100,000,000 founder shares of Class A Common Stock and 10,000,000 founder shares of Class B Common Stock to Mr. Ra&#250;l Lahud Quiroz, our Chief Executive Officer, at par value ($110 in aggregate).&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>In 2024, we issued 8,800,000 shares of Class A Common Stock under Board Advisory Agreements to Adamson Brothers, Corp. in consideration of advisory services, which Adamson Brothers, Corp. then assigned to Spire Capital Limited; we recorded consulting expense of $9. The shares are held of record by Spire Capital Limited.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On August 16, 2024, we commenced a private placement under Rule 506(b) of Regulation D and Regulation S to raise up to $500,000. During 2024, we issued 132,800 shares of Class A Common Stock at $0.10 per share for gross proceeds of $13,280 and received $760 of subscriptions for 7,600 additional shares. Offering costs totaled $89,240, of which $13,280 was charged against equity and $75,960 was recorded as financing expense. We filed notices of the offering on Form D with the SEC on January 24, 2025 and February 23, 2026.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On May 6, 2025, we issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock to Mr. Lahud in exchange for 99 of the 100 outstanding shares of BRA, under the Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement dated April 22, 2025.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On May 6, 2025, we issued 6,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock to four consultants, with an aggregate fair value of $600,000, for services to be rendered from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>During 2025, we cancelled 8,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issued in 2024 for which proceeds had not been received, and between November 13 and December 2, 2025 we issued 8,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at $0.10 per share to seventeen non-U.S. investors under Regulation S for proceeds of $800. We also received $800 of subscriptions for 100 shares at $8.00 per share, which had not been issued at June 30, 2026, and refunded $220 of overpayments received in 2024.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>In the first quarter of 2026 (approved January 10, 2026 and recorded by our transfer agent on February 22, 2026), we issued 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock, with a fair value of $217,866, to Silver Rock Group as the commitment fee under the Share Purchase Agreement dated August 29, 2024.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>In the first quarter of 2026 (approved January 10, 2026 and recorded by our transfer agent on February 22, 2026), we issued 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock, with a fair value of $5,426,066, to Mr. Juan Pablo Mu&#241;oz Flores as consideration for the agricultural properties acquired by BRA in the BRA Land Acquisition.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>On June 26, 2026, pursuant to a unanimous written consent of our board of directors of that date, we issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share, with an aggregate value of $315,416, to Mr. Lahud, as directed by the creditor, in settlement of $315,421 of advances owed to Lahud150, S.A. de C.V., a company controlled by our Chief Executive Officer. The remaining $5 was waived by the creditor and treated as a capital contribution to the Company. The shares were issued in reliance on Regulation S and Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act, are restricted securities and bear a restrictive legend.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>No securities were issued between June 30, 2026 and the date of this Amendment.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 11. DESCRIPTION OF REGISTRANT&#8217;S SECURITIES TO BE REGISTERED</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The following summary of the material terms of our capital stock is qualified in its entirety by reference to our Certificate of Incorporation and our Bylaws, which are filed as exhibits to this registration statement, and to the applicable provisions of the Delaware General Corporation Law (the &#8220;DGCL&#8221;). We are registering our Class A Common Stock under Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Authorized Capital Stock</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our Certificate of Incorporation authorizes the issuance of the following classes of capital stock, each with a par value of $0.000001 per share:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Class A Common Stock:</B> 800,000,000 shares authorized, of which 123,650,883 shares were issued and outstanding as of November 4, 2026, held by 306 holders of record. Each share carries one vote.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Class B Common Stock:</B> 50,000,000 shares authorized, of which 10,000,000 shares were issued and outstanding as of November 4, 2026, all held by Mr. Lahud. Each share carries twenty votes.&nbsp;</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>33</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Class C Common Stock:</B> 75,000,000 shares authorized, none of which is outstanding. Class C shares carry no voting rights.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD><B>Preferred Stock:</B> 75,000,000 shares authorized, none of which is outstanding. Preferred shares carry no voting rights.&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Class A Common Stock</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Voting.</B> Each holder of Class A Common Stock is entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders. Holders of Class A Common Stock vote together with holders of Class B Common Stock as a single class, except as otherwise required by the DGCL. Voting rights are not cumulative, so the holders of a majority of the voting power can elect all of the directors standing for election. Because the Class B Common Stock carries twenty votes per share, holders of Class A Common Stock, voting as a group, do not currently have the power to elect any director or approve any matter without the concurrence of Mr. Lahud. See &#8220;Class B Common Stock&#8221; below.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Dividends.</B> Subject to the rights of any Preferred Stock that may be issued, holders of Class A Common Stock are entitled to share equally, on a per-share basis with the other classes of common stock, in dividends when, as and if declared by our board of directors out of funds legally available for that purpose.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Liquidation.</B> Upon our liquidation, dissolution or winding up, whether voluntary or involuntary, holders of Class A Common Stock are entitled to share equally, on a per-share basis with the other classes of common stock, in the assets available for distribution to common stockholders after payment of our liabilities and of any liquidation preference of outstanding Preferred Stock.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Other rights.</B> Holders of Class A Common Stock have no preemptive, subscription, redemption, sinking fund or conversion rights. All outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock are fully paid and non-assessable.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Class B Common Stock</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Each share of Class B Common Stock carries twenty votes per share on all matters submitted to stockholders and otherwise has the same dividend and liquidation rights as the Class A Common Stock. In addition, Article III, Section E of our Certificate of Incorporation provides that the Class B &#8220;controlling shares with controlling interest shall be entitled to maintain veto power over any board vote,&#8221; and that &#8220;the individual representing Class B effectively can make board decisions on their own, including hiring C-level executives.&#8221; The Class B Common Stock is not convertible into Class A Common Stock and does not automatically convert upon transfer. All 10,000,000 outstanding shares of Class B Common Stock are held by Mr. Lahud. As a result, Mr. Lahud controls approximately 94.2% of our voting power and, through the Class B veto right, the decisions of our board of directors. See &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors.&#8221;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Class C Common Stock and Preferred Stock</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Shares of Class C Common Stock have no voting rights but otherwise share equally with the other classes of common stock in dividends and distributions. Our board of directors has the authority, without further action by the stockholders, to issue shares of Preferred Stock in one or more series and to fix the dividend rights, liquidation preferences, conversion rights, redemption terms and other rights, preferences and restrictions of each series, except that under our Certificate of Incorporation the Preferred Stock carries no voting rights. Preferred Stock, if issued, could have dividend and liquidation rights senior to the common stock and could be used to delay, deter or prevent a change in control. No series of Preferred Stock has been designated.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Anti-Takeover Provisions</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Section 203 of the DGCL.</B> Our Certificate of Incorporation does not opt out of Section 203 of the DGCL, which, subject to certain exceptions, prohibits a Delaware corporation from engaging in a &#8220;business combination&#8221; with an &#8220;interested stockholder&#8221; (generally, a person who owns 15% or more of the corporation&#8217;s outstanding voting stock) for three years following the time that person became an interested stockholder, unless the business combination or the acquisition of shares is approved in a prescribed manner.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Dual-class structure and Class B veto.</B> The twenty-vote-per-share Class B Common Stock and the Class B veto over board decisions concentrate control in Mr. Lahud and would make it impossible for a third party to acquire control of the Company, or to replace our board of directors, without his consent.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>34</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B>Bylaws.</B> Our Bylaws provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by the board of directors, and that stockholders may act by written consent in lieu of a meeting. Our Certificate of Incorporation authorizes the board to issue Preferred Stock without stockholder approval.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Listing</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>On March 6, 2026, we submitted an application to list our Class A Common Stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol &#8220;BCRP.&#8221; The application is pending. No assurance can be given that our application will be approved; as described under &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors,&#8221; we do not currently satisfy the initial listing requirements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>Transfer Agent and Registrar</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The transfer agent and registrar for our common stock is VStock Transfer, LLC, 18 Lafayette Place, Woodmere, New York 11598; telephone +1 (212) 828-8436.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>ITEM 12. INDEMNIFICATION OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Section 145 of the DGCL authorizes a corporation to indemnify its directors, officers, employees and agents against expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees), judgments, fines and amounts paid in settlement actually and reasonably incurred in connection with any threatened, pending or completed action, suit or proceeding (other than an action by or in the right of the corporation) to which the person is or is threatened to be made a party by reason of the fact that the person is or was a director, officer, employee or agent of the corporation, if the person acted in good faith and in a manner the person reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the corporation and, with respect to any criminal action or proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe the conduct was unlawful. In an action by or in the right of the corporation, indemnification is limited to expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees) and is not permitted in respect of any claim as to which the person has been adjudged liable to the corporation unless, and only to the extent that, the Court of Chancery or the court in which the action was brought determines that the person is fairly and reasonably entitled to indemnity. Section 145 further provides that a director or officer who has been successful on the merits or otherwise in defense of any such action, suit or proceeding must be indemnified against expenses actually and reasonably incurred, that indemnification (unless ordered by a court) must be authorized upon a determination that the applicable standard of conduct has been met by a majority of disinterested directors, a committee of such directors, independent legal counsel or the stockholders, that expenses may be advanced upon receipt of an undertaking to repay, and that a corporation may purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of any such person against any liability asserted against the person in that capacity, whether or not the corporation would have the power to indemnify the person against such liability.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Section 102(b)(7) of the DGCL permits a corporation to include in its certificate of incorporation a provision eliminating or limiting the personal liability of directors and officers to the corporation or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty, except for liability (i) for any breach of the duty of loyalty, (ii) for acts or omissions not in good faith or which involve intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law, (iii) under Section 174 of the DGCL (unlawful dividends or stock repurchases), (iv) for any transaction from which the director or officer derived an improper personal benefit, or (v) in the case of officers, in any action by or in the right of the corporation. Our Certificate of Incorporation does not currently contain such a provision.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Our Bylaws provide that we shall indemnify our directors and officers to the fullest extent authorized by the DGCL, subject to the limitations set forth therein. We have not entered into indemnification agreements with our directors and officers and do not currently maintain directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance, but we expect to do so in connection with our planned listing.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Insofar as indemnification for liabilities arising under the Securities Act may be permitted to directors, officers or persons controlling the Company pursuant to the foregoing provisions, we have been informed that in the opinion of the SEC such indemnification is against public policy as expressed in the Securities Act and is therefore unenforceable.</P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0.05pt;margin-bottom:6pt;color:#000000'><B>REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</B></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:11.3pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:17.95pt'>To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of Biointra, Corp.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:17.95pt;color:#000000'><B>Opinion on the Financial Statements</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5.9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:-0.05pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.6pt'>We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Biointra, Corp. (&#8220;the Company&#8221;) as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, and the related consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss, stockholders&#8217; deficit, and cash flows for each of the two years in the period ended December 31, 2025, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the financial statements). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2025, and 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the two years in the period ended December 31, 2025, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:18pt;color:#000000'><B>Going Concern</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6.05pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.75pt'>The accompanying financial statements have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern. As discussed in Note 13 to the financial statements, the Company has not yet achieved profitable operations, expects to incur further losses in the development of its business, has a significant accumulated deficit, and does not have sufficient cash to meet obligations. These factors, among others, raise substantial doubt about the Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. Management&#8217;s plans in regard to these matters are also described in Note 13. The financial statements do not include any adjustments that might result from the outcome of this uncertainty.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5.95pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:18pt;color:#000000'><B>Basis for Opinion</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.75pt'>These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6.05pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.75pt'>We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB and in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States of America. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits, we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.6pt'>Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</P>
<P style='font:11pt Times New Roman;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:18pt;color:#000000'><B>Critical Audit Matters</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5.9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:17.65pt'>The critical audit matters communicated below are matters arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that were communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relate to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The communication of critical audit matters does not alter in any way our opinion on the financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matters below, providing separate opinions on the critical audit matters or on the accounts or disclosures to which they relate.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>40</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
</DIV>
<DIV><HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:2.3pt;margin-bottom:0pt'><B><I>Valuation of Acquired Property (Note 4 to the Financial Statements)</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5.9pt;margin-bottom:0pt'><I>Description of the Critical Audit Matter</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0.05pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:17.65pt'>During 2025, the Company acquired agricultural property, including land, bearer plants, buildings and improvements, irrigation and hydraulic infrastructure, and water rights. Management determined the fair value of the acquired property using third-party appraisal reports, which included market comparable data, replacement-cost inputs, crop/tree valuation inputs, water-right valuation inputs, and condition, age, conservation, and obsolescence factors. Auditing the valuation of the acquired property involved a high degree of auditor judgment and effort due to the nature of the acquisition and the subjectivity involved in evaluating the valuation methodologies and significant inputs utilized by management and the appraiser.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0.05pt;margin-bottom:0pt'><I>How the Critical Audit Matter Was Addressed in the Audit</I></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our principal audit procedures related to the valuation of the acquired property included the following:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Symbol;margin:0;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:17.9pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18.05pt'>&#183;</KBD><FONT style='font-family:Times New Roman'>We evaluated management&#8217;s use of the third-party appraisal reports, including the valuation methodologies applied and the competence, capabilities, and objectivity of the appraiser.</FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Symbol;margin:0;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:17.75pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'>&#183;</KBD><FONT style='font-family:Times New Roman'>We tested the reasonableness of the significant valuation inputs and assumptions by tracing key source data to purchase agreements, notarized deeds, market comparables, regional construction and agricultural cost data, supplier information, and other supporting evidence.</FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Symbol;margin:0;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:17.75pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'>&#183;</KBD><FONT style='font-family:Times New Roman'>We evaluated the relevance and reliability of significant data used in the valuation by considering the source, nature, and corroboration of the underlying market, contractual, and third-party information. We also evaluated whether the resulting recognition, classification, and allocation of the acquired assets, including land, bearer plants, buildings, land improvements, and water licenses, were appropriate under U.S. GAAP.</FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:11pt><B>Biointra, Corp.</B></FONT></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><B>Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:9pt><B>For the year ended December 31, 2025 and the period from May 8, 2024 (inception) to December 31, 2024</B></FONT></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:9pt><B>(Expressed in U.S. dollars)</B></FONT></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 1 &#8211;&nbsp;NATURE OF OPERATIONS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Biointra, Corp. was incorporated in Delaware on May 8, 2024 (the &#8220;Company&#8221;). The Company is in the business of developing integrated solutions for the recovery and beneficial use of organic waste, including renewable-energy-related initiatives, with operations concentrated in Mexico. In connection with this strategy, through its wholly owned subsidiary, the Company acquired agricultural properties in Mexico that include land, agricultural improvements, water rights, buildings, and avocado and blue agave bearer plants. These properties are under active cultivation. The agricultural operations are intended to preserve and develop the productive value of the acquired properties and provide operational flexibility and potential agricultural inputs and cash flows while the Company continues to develop its broader renewable-energy and organic-waste recovery initiatives.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>To date, the Company&#8217;s activities have principally consisted of raising capital, organizational matters, development of its business plan, and activities related to the acquired agricultural properties. The Company has not generated revenue since inception.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 2 &#8211;&nbsp;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Basis of Presentation and Principles of Consolidation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The accounting and reporting policies of the Company conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). In the opinion of management, all adjustments considered necessary for the fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements for the period presented have been included. The Company&#8217;s fiscal year end is December 31.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco SAPI DE CV (&#8220;BRA&#8221;). All inter-company transactions and balances have been eliminated upon consolidation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Use of Estimates</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and the footnotes thereto. Actual results could differ from those estimates. It is reasonably possible that changes in estimates will occur in the near term. All amounts are rounded to the nearest whole dollar upon presentation so certain sums or differences may reflect a rounding difference in some instances.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Examples of reported amounts that rely on significant estimates include certain amounts relating to the accounting for acquired agricultural property and equipment, inventory, income taxes, including valuation allowance, and stock-based compensation expense.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Risks and Uncertainties</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has a limited operating history. The Company&#8217;s business and operations are sensitive to general business and economic conditions in the United States and Mexico. A host of factors beyond the Company&#8217;s control could cause fluctuations in these conditions. Adverse conditions may include: recession, downturn or otherwise, local market competition, changing consumer preferences, unpredictable climate patterns, and agricultural yield volatility. These adverse conditions could affect the Company&#8217;s financial condition and the results of its operations. As of December 31, 2025, the Company is operating as a going concern. See Note 13 for additional information.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company considers short-term, highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase to be cash equivalents. Cash consists of funds held in the Company&#8217;s checking account. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had $33,931 and $9,989 of cash on hand, respectively.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-7</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Agricultural Inventories and Growing Crops.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value. Cost is determined on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis, with the acquisition cost of each acquired plantation and the cultivation costs capitalized to it identified by plantation. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Unharvested Growing Agave: All direct and indirect agricultural costs incurred to acquire, plant, cultivate, and maintain agave fields prior to maturity are capitalized and deferred as work-in-process inventory. &nbsp;Due to the multi-year maturation timeline, growing crops expected to be harvested beyond 12 months from the balance sheet date are classified as non-current assets.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Harvested Agave: Upon harvest, when the leaves are sheared and the agave core (pi&#241;a) is removed from the field, the capitalized cultivation costs under ASC 905-330-35-1, together with the allocated acquisition cost of the plantation and net of any previously recognized inventory write-downs, are transferred to harvested crop inventory, which consists of agave pi&#241;as held for sale to tequila producers and is not used in any further production process of the Company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Net realizable value represents the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal, and transportation. The Company evaluates the carrying value of its agricultural assets regularly, recording write-downs for crop damage, spoilage, or market declines directly to the operating expense in the period they occur. &nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Property and Equipment</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Property and equipment are stated at cost, net of accumulated depreciation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company&#8217;s property and equipment consists of land, land improvements, buildings and bearer plants. The fair value of the land (both cultivated and uncultivated) was estimated based on comparable transactions for similar agricultural properties, adjusted for location, size, accessibility, agronomic conditions, and infrastructure. For land improvements and buildings, fair value was determined using replacement costs adjusted for asset condition. The fair value of bearer plants was based on initial establishment costs plus accumulated pre-productive and productive-stage maintenance costs. These costs were referenced from Fideicomisos Instituidos en Relaci&#243;n con la Agricultura (FIRA), a Mexican federal development bank supporting the agricultural and rural sectors.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Depreciation of the land improvement is calculated on a straight-line method over the estimated useful life of 4 years. Depreciation of the buildings is calculated on a straight-line method over the estimated useful life of 20 years. Depreciation of the bearer plants is calculated on a straight-line method over the estimated production life of 4 years.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Definite-lived Intangible Assets</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Intangible assets acquired are recognized at cost. These assets are then amortized over their estimated useful lives, reflecting the pattern of economic benefits derived from the assets. Specifically, water licenses are amortized using the straight-line method over their contractual useful lives. The Company&#8217;s water concession has an initial legal term of 10 years and may be renewed for additional 10-year periods, subject to timely renewal and compliance with applicable legal requirements.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment and definite-lived intangible assets are held for use and are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable. Such events or changes may include insufficient cash flows, changes in business plans, or plans to dispose of assets before the end of their estimated useful or production lives. We first group individual assets based on the lowest level for which identifiable cash flows are largely independent of the cash flows from other assets. Recoverability is assessed by comparing the carrying amount of the asset group to the sum of the estimated undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use and eventual disposition of the asset group. If the undiscounted cash flows are less than the carrying amount, an impairment loss is recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the asset group&#8217;s fair value. Fair value is determined using discounted cash flow analyses, which incorporate significant management estimates and assumptions, including forecasts of future operating performance (such as revenue growth rates and expected profitability margins), estimates of the remaining useful or production lives and service potential of the assets within the asset group, and a discount rate based on the Company&#8217;s weighted-average cost of capital.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>There was no impairment loss recognized in the year ended December 31, 2025.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Deferred Financing Costs</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company records financing costs in accordance with ASC 340-10-S99-1. Deferred financing costs consist of legal, accounting, and other costs (including underwriting discounts and commissions) incurred through the balance sheet date that are directly related to the S-1 registration statement and that will be charged to stockholders&#8217; equity upon the completion of the </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-8</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>initial public offering (&#8220;IPO&#8221;). Should the IPO prove to be unsuccessful, these deferred costs, as well as additional expenses to be incurred, will be charged to operations.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Stock-based Compensation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with ASC 718. Stock-based compensation expense for equity instruments issued to employees and non-employees is measured based on the grant-date fair value of the awards. The fair value of each stock unit is determined based on the valuation of the Company&#8217;s stock on the date of grant. The Company recognizes compensation costs using the straight-line method for equity compensation awards over the requisite service period of the awards, which is generally the awards&#8217; vesting period.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Fair Value Measurements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company follows guidance for accounting for fair value measurements of financial assets and financial liabilities and for fair value measurements of non-financial items that are recognized or disclosed at fair value in the financial statements on a recurring basis. Additionally, the Company adopted guidance for fair value measurement related to non-financial items that are recognized and disclosed at fair value in the consolidated financial statements on a non-recurring basis. The guidance establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to measurements involving significant unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are as follows:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>Level 1 inputs are quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the Company has the ability to access at the measurement date.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>Level 2 inputs are inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:4pt;margin-left:27pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-left:-13.5pt'>&#8226;</KBD>Level 3 inputs are unobservable inputs for the asset or liability. The carrying amounts of financial assets such as cash approximate their fair values because of the short maturity of these instruments.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Earnings (Loss) Per Share</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic 260, <I>Earnings per Share</I> (&#8220;ASC 260&#8221;) requires a company that has participating security holders to utilize the two-class method for calculating earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) unless the treasury stock method results in lower EPS. The two-class method is an allocation of earnings/(loss) between the holders of common stock and a company&#8217;s participating security holders. Under the two-class method, earnings/(loss) for the reporting period are allocated between common stockholders and other security holders based on their respective rights to receive distributed earnings (i.e., dividends) and undistributed earnings (i.e., net income/(loss)). Basic EPS is calculated by dividing income or loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding, excluding participating shares in accordance with ASC 260. Diluted EPS gives effect to all dilutive potential common shares outstanding during the period using the treasury stock method. In computing diluted EPS, the average stock price for the period is used in determining the number of shares assumed to be purchased from the exercise of stock options or warrants. Diluted EPS excludes all dilutive potential shares if their effect is anti-dilutive. As at December 31, 2025, the Company had 3,692,556 (2024 &#8211;&nbsp;2,186,256) potentially dilutive Class A shares outstanding. Potentially dilutive shares at December 31, 2025 and 2024 were excluded from the earnings per share calculation as their impact would have been anti-dilutive.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Income Taxes</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Income taxes are provided for the tax effects of transactions reported in the consolidated financial statements and consist of taxes currently due plus deferred taxes related primarily to differences between the basis of receivables, property and equipment, intangible assets, and accrued expenses for financial and income tax reporting. The deferred tax assets and liabilities represent the future tax return consequences of those differences, which will either be taxable or deductible when the assets and liabilities are recovered or settled. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>For the current period, the Company is taxed as a C corporation. The Company evaluates its tax positions that have been taken or are expected to be taken on income tax returns to determine if an accrual is necessary for uncertain tax positions. As of December 31, 2025, the unrecognized tax benefits accrual was zero.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-9</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company conducts business globally and, as a result, files income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and various state and foreign jurisdictions. In the normal course of business, the Company is subject to examination by taxing authorities throughout the world.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Foreign Currency Translation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The consolidated financial statements are presented in United States dollars which is the parent&#8217;s functional and reporting currency. The functional currency of BRA is the Mexico Peso. Management applies ASC 830, Foreign Currency Matters. In accordance with ASC 830-30-45-3, all assets and liabilities of BRA are translated into United States dollars at the exchange rate prevailing at the balance sheet date, equity accounts are translated at historical rates, and revenues and expenses are translated at average monthly rates. The resulting translation adjustments are reported as a component of other comprehensive income (loss) and accumulated in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) in stockholders&#8217; equity. Transactions denominated in a currency other than an entity&#8217;s functional currency are remeasured into the functional currency at the exchange rate in effect on the transaction date, and monetary balances so denominated are remeasured at the balance sheet date, with the resulting gains and losses included in net loss.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Advertising and Marketing Expenses</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company expenses advertising and marketing costs as they are incurred. The amounts incurred in 2025 was $495 (2024 - $3,600).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Organizational Costs</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In accordance with ASC 720-15-25-1, <I>Other Expenses</I>, organizational costs, including consulting fees, transfer agent fees, accounting fees, legal fee, and costs of incorporation, are expensed as incurred.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Segment Reporting</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In accordance with ASC 280, <I>Segment Reporting</I>, operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise for which separate discrete information is available for evaluation by the chief operating decision maker in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance (the &#8220;CODM&#8221;). For the Company, its CODM is its Chief Executive Officer. The Company views its operations and manages its business as one operating and reporting segment. This single segment reflects the Company&#8217;s core business, which is the development of solutions to recycle organic waste for the production of renewable energy, and is operated in two geographical areas (U.S.A. and Mexico).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The CODM assesses the Company&#8217;s operating and financial performance based on operating expenses during fiscal year 2025, but revenues, net income, and return on investment will be significant factors to be assessed once the Company commences operations.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-09, Income Taxes (Topic 740): <I>Improvement to Income Tax Disclosures</I> to enhance the transparency of income tax disclosures relating to the rate reconciliation, disclosure of income taxes paid, and certain other disclosures. The ASU should be applied prospectively and is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2024, with early adoption permitted. The adoption of this ASU did not have any material effects on its financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Recent Accounting Pronouncements Not Yet Adopted</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, <I>Income Statement &#8211;&nbsp;Reporting Comprehensive Income &#8211;&nbsp;Expense Disaggregation Disclosure (Subtopic 220-40)</I>. The amendments in this update enhance disclosures about a public business entity&#8217;s expenses and provide more detailed information about the types of expenses included in certain notes in the consolidated financial statements. ASU 2024-03 is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and interim reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2027. Early adoption permitted. The amendments may be applied prospectively to reporting periods after the effective date or retrospectively to all periods presented in the consolidated financial statements. The Company is currently evaluating any new disclosures that may be required upon adoption of ASU 2024-03.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company&#8217;s management does not believe that any recently issued, but not yet effective, accounting standards, if currently adopted, would have a material effect on the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-10</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 3 &#8211;&nbsp;ACQUISITION OF BIOINTRA RENOVABLES ATOTONILCO JALISCO SAPI DE CV</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On April 22, 2025, the Company entered into a Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco SAPI DE CV. (&#8220;BRA&#8221;), a Mexican corporation controlled by the CEO of the Company. Pursuant to the agreement, the Company issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company on May 6, 2025 to acquire all of the outstanding shares of BRA. The Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement closed upon the Company obtaining control of BRA on August 8, 2025. Pursuant to ASC 805-50-30-5, the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition under common control. The transfer of the net assets or equity interest from BRA does not constitute a business and therefore would not represent a change in the reporting entity. At the closing of the acquisition, the Company recognized the net assets of BRA at the historical carrying value of $421 and began reporting the net assets transferred in its consolidated financial statements prospectively from the date of the transfer. The difference between the fair value of shares of Class A Common Stock issued and the net assets or equity interests of BRA is included in additional paid-in capital at December 31, 2025.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 4 &#8211;&nbsp;REAL PROPERTY PURCHASE AGREEMENT</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On September 15, 2025, BRA entered into a Real Property Purchase Agreement to acquire certain agricultural property assets which consists of land, land improvements, water licenses and avocado and agave plantations including buildings and bearer plants, with a fair value of $5,426,066 (MXN99,652,094) in consideration for 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company. The fair value of the consideration payable was determined based on third-party appraisals of assets acquired along with observable market data from transactions between normal market participants. BRA obtained control of the agricultural property assets upon execution of the Real Property Purchase Agreement, and the agricultural property is currently under active cultivation with developing crops. As at December 31, 2025, the common shares have not been issued. Refer to Note 6, Note 7 and Note 8 for the details of assets acquired in the transaction.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 5 &#8211;&nbsp;DEFERRED FINANCING COSTS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded $65,000 (period ended December 31, 2024 - $45,000) of deferred financing costs related to its S-1 registration statement.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:-0.5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 6 &#8211;&nbsp;INVENTORY</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:-0.5pt;color:#000000'>Inventory consisted of unharvested agave plantations acquired from the BRA transaction (Note 4). As at December 31, 2025, the agave plants are approximately 6 years old, and the Company expected to harvest them within the following 12 months. &nbsp;A continuity of the Company&#8217;s inventory assets as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 is as follows:</P>

</TABLE>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized a loss of $559,798 from the write-down of inventory to net realizable value. The write-down arose because the market price of bulk blue agave in Mexico declined substantially during 2025 as a result of an oversupply of mature plants in the Tequila Denomination of Origin region, such that the cost allocated to the agave plantations on acquisition (which was based on the replacement cost of a six-year-old plant) exceeded the amount expected to be realized on harvest.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Net realizable value was measured as at December 31, 2025 on a plantation-by-plantation basis, using the following principal assumptions:</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'>&#183;</KBD><I>Expected harvest quantities.</I> An estimated 2,371 metric tons of agave pi&#241;a standing on 28.92 hectares (approximately 101,207 plants), comprising approximately 1,476 tons at the Las Lomas plantation in Tequila, Jalisco and approximately 895 tons at the Ejido Mojarritas plantation in Santa Mar&#237;a del Oro, Nayarit. The estimate is based on the independent agricultural appraisals of the two properties, which apply a yield of 82 tons per hectare.&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'>&#183;</KBD><I>Estimated selling price.</I> MXN 8.00 per kilogram, being the going price in December 2025 paid by tequila producers to registered growers under supply contracts and the CRT/CNIT &#8220;Agave Responsable Social&#8221; scheme (reported &nbsp;</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-11</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-left:36pt'>range MXN 6.00&#8211;8.00 per kilogram). Both plantations are registered with the Consejo Regulador del Tequila and lie within the Denomination of Origin zone, and management expects to sell the crop to distilleries through that contract channel in the ordinary course of business. Prices obtainable in the spot or intermediary market (approximately MXN 2.00&#8211;5.00 per kilogram in December 2025) were not used, as they do not represent the channel available to the Company.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'>&#183;</KBD><I>Remaining costs of completion, harvesting, transportation and disposal.</I> The plantations are mature and no further cultivation costs are required. Estimated costs to cut, trim and load the pi&#241;as (jima) and to transport them to the distilleries were MXN 1.50 per kilogram for Las Lomas (approximately 12 kilometers from the Tequila distillery corridor) and MXN 2.00 per kilogram for Mojarritas (approximately 150 kilometers from the distilleries), based on regional contractor rates.&nbsp;</P>

<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 9 &#8211;&nbsp;INCOME TAX PROVISION</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company accounts for income taxes as set forth in ASC 740, <I>Income Taxes</I>. Deferred taxes are determined based on the temporary differences between the consolidated financial statement and tax basis of assets and liabilities using tax rates expected to be in effect during the years in which the basis differences reverse. A valuation allowance is recorded when it is unlikely that the deferred tax assets will be realized.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company is taxed as a corporation and is subject to income taxation in the United States and in Mexico through its wholly-owned foreign subsidiary. Losses before income taxes are generated in both jurisdictions and the Company&#8217;s income tax expense (benefit) is affected by the differences between the U.S. federal statutory income tax rate and the statutory tax rate applicable in Mexico. Accordingly, the reconciliation of income tax expense (benefit) at the U.S. federal statutory rate to the Company&#8217;s reported income tax expense (benefit) includes the effect of foreign operations, including the impact of losses incurred in Mexico.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company assesses its income tax positions and records tax benefits for all years subject to examination based upon its evaluation of the facts, circumstances and information available at the reporting date. In accordance with ASC 740-10, for those tax positions where there is a greater than 50% likelihood that a tax benefit will be sustained, our policy is to record the largest amount of tax benefit that is more likely than not to be realized upon ultimate settlement with a taxing authority that has full knowledge of all relevant information. For those income tax positions where there is less than 50% likelihood that a tax benefit will be sustained, no tax benefit will be recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The Company has determined that there are no material uncertain tax positions.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company accounts for income taxes with the recognition of estimated income taxes payable or refundable on income tax returns for the current period and for the estimated future tax effect attributable to temporary differences and carryforwards. Measurement of deferred income items is based on enacted tax laws including tax rates, with the measurement of deferred income tax assets being reduced by available tax benefits not expected to be realized in the immediate future. No benefit (provision) has been recognized for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. The US and Mexico components of net loss for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 are as follows:</P>
<TABLE align=center style=border-collapse:collapse;width:100%><TR><TD valign=bottom style=padding-top:1.5pt;padding-left:3pt;padding-bottom:1.5pt;padding-right:3pt><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Due to uncertainty as to the Company&#8217;s ability to generate sufficient taxable income in the future to utilize the net operating loss carryforwards, the Company has recorded a full valuation allowance to reduce the net deferred tax asset to zero, on the face of the consolidated financial statements. The Company&#8217;s net operating loss deduction in the United States is limited to </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-13</FONT></P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>80% of taxable income in any given carryforward year. The Company&#8217;s net operating losses incurred in Mexico can be carried forward and deducted from income earned for up to 10 years. The 2025 tax returns in the United States and Mexico have not yet been filed as of the issuance of these consolidated financial statements. All tax periods since inception remain open to examination by the taxing jurisdictions to which the Company is subject.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 10 &#8211;&nbsp;STOCKHOLDERS&#8217; DEFICIT</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Common Stock</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has 3 classes of Common Stock; Class A, Class B and Class C.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 800,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has 119,932,800 Class A Common Stock outstanding as of December 31, 2025 (2024 &#8211;&nbsp;108,932,800). Each Class A Common Stock is entitled to 1 vote per share.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 50,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has 10,000,000 Class B Common Stock outstanding as of December 31, 2025 (2024 &#8211;&nbsp;10,000,000). Each Class B Common Stock is entitled to 20 votes per share.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 75,000,000 Class C Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has not issued any Class C Common Stock as of December 31, 2025. Shares of Class C Common Stock have no voting power.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><I>During the year ended December 31, 2025:</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On May 6, 2025, the Company issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company in exchange for the net assets of BRA, which were recorded at their historical carrying value of $421 rather than at the fair value of the shares issued, pursuant to the Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA (Note 3).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On May 6, 2025, the Company issued 6,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at a fair value of $600,000 for services to be rendered for the period from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded consulting expense of $350,000 on the statements of operations and comprehensive loss. At December 31, 2025, the Company recorded prepaid consulting expenses of $250,000 on the consolidated balance sheet.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company cancelled 8,000 shares of Class A Common Stock issued during the period ended December 31, 2024 as the Company did not receive the proceeds from the subscribers. The Company then reissued 8,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at $0.10 per share for cash proceeds of $800.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company received proceeds from Class A Common Stock subscriptions in the amount of $800 for 100 shares at $8 per share. The Company also refunded $220 of overpayment received from subscribers during the period ended December 31, 2024 which was for the subscription of 2,200 shares of Class A Common Stock.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>As at December 31, 2025, 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company are issuable related to the acquisition of certain agricultural property assets which consists of land, land improvements, water licenses and avocado and agave plantations including buildings and bearer plants, with a fair value of $5,426,066 (MXN99,652,094) (Note 4).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><I>During the period ended December 31, 2024:</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company issued 100,000,000 Founder shares of Class A Common Stock to the CEO of the Company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company issued 10,000,000 Founder shares of Class B Common Stock to the CEO of the Company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company issued 8,800,000 shares of Class A Common Stock pursuant to Board Advisory Agreements and recorded consulting expense of $9 on the statement of operations and comprehensive loss.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company issued 132,800 shares of Class A Common Stock at $0.10 per share for cash proceeds of $13,280. In connection with the share issuance, the Company incurred offering costs of $89,240, of which $13,280 was netted against the proceeds received and the remaining $75,960 was recorded as financing expense in the statement of operations and comprehensive loss. The $13,280 of proceeds from the share issuance represents the maximum amount the Company could charge against equity, with the remaining expensed in the statement of operations and comprehensive loss.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company received $760 for subscriptions of 7,600 shares of Class A Common Stock and recorded offering costs of $760.</P>
