<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 11 &#8211;&nbsp;RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS AND BALANCES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>All transactions with related parties have occurred in the normal course of operations and are recorded at the exchange amount which is the amount agreed to by the Company and the related parties.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On August 8, 2025, the Company closed a Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA, a Mexican corporation controlled by the CEO of the Company which is accounted for as an asset acquisition under common control pursuant to ASC 805-50-30-5. On May 6, 2025, the Company issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company to acquire all of the outstanding shares of BRA. The Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement closed upon the Company obtaining control of BRA on August 8, 2025. Refer to Note 3.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>As at December 31, 2025, the Company owed $224,274 (2024 - $100,390) to a company controlled by the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) of the Company which represents cash advances, deferred financing costs, prepaid consulting fees, and general and administrative expenses incurred on behalf of the Company. The amount is non-interest bearing, unsecured and due on demand.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 12 &#8211;&nbsp;SEGMENT REPORTING</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company views its operations and manages its business as one operating and reporting segment. This single segment reflects the Company&#8217;s core business, which is the development of solutions to recycle organic waste for the production of renewable energy, and is operated in two geographical areas (U.S.A. and Mexico).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company&#8217;s Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;), who is the Chief Executive Officer, evaluates financial performance and allocates resources on a consolidated basis. The CODM uses consolidated operating loss, net loss, and cash flow information to assess performance and make decisions regarding the allocation of resources. As these financial measures are reviewed on a consolidated basis, the Company has determined that it has a single operating and reporting segment.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company operates in two geographical areas of U.S.A. and Mexico. The Company&#8217;s property and equipment, and intangible assets, by geographical areas as at December 31, 2025, were all located in Mexico.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 13 &#8211;&nbsp;GOING CONCERN</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>These consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles applicable to a going concern, which assumes that the Company will be able to meet its obligations and continue its operations for a period of at least one year from the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements. Realization values may be substantially different from carrying values as shown and these consolidated financial statements do not give effect to adjustments that would be necessary to the carrying values and classification of assets and liabilities should the Company be unable to continue as a going concern. At December 31, 2025, the Company had not yet achieved profitable operations and expects to incur further losses in the development of its business. As reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements, the Company had an accumulated deficit of $1,297,077 at December 31, 2025. This factor among others raises substantial doubt about the Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. The Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern is dependent upon its ability to generate future profitable operations and/or to obtain the necessary financing to meet its obligations and repay its liabilities arising from normal business operations when they come due. Management has no formal plan in place to address this concern but considers that the Company will be able to obtain additional funds by equity financing and/or related party advances, however, there is no assurance of additional funding being available.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 14 &#8211;&nbsp;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Share Purchase Agreement</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On August 29, 2024, the Company entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Silver Rock Group (&#8220;Silver Rock&#8221;) whereby Silver Rock committed to purchase up to $350,000,000 of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock (the &#8220;Draw Down Amount&#8221;) over a 36-month period beginning on the date the Company becomes publicly listed (&#8220;Public Listing&#8221;). The agreement provides the Company with the right, at its sole discretion, to issue Draw Down Notices in tranches of up to one million shares at a per-share price equal to a 10% discount to the lowest trading price of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock during the 10 trading </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-15</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>days immediately preceding the Draw Down Notice. The Draw Down Amount requested shall not exceed 200% or one million dollars of the average daily trading volume for the 10 trading days immediately preceding the draw down exercise date on a rolling basis.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In connection with the Share Purchase Agreement, the Company agreed to pay a commitment fee equal to 2% of the total outstanding shares of the Company on the date of the agreement. During the period ended December 31, 2024, the Company recorded a commitment fee of $217,866 on the statement of operations and comprehensive loss for 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock. The fair value of the 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock is included in shares issuable at December 31, 2025.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In addition, on the date of Public Listing, the Company shall issue share purchase warrants to Silver Rock granting the right to purchase additional common shares of the Company for a period of 5 years at an exercise price per share equal to the lower of $2 per share or 110% of the listing price immediately after the Public Listing. The number of warrants issued shall be equal to 4% of the total outstanding shares immediately after the completion of the Public Listing, calculated on a fully diluted basis. As at December 31, 2025 and the issuance date of the consolidated financial statements, the Company has not become publicly listed. As a result, the number of warrants to be issued and its fair value are indeterminable.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 15 &#8211;&nbsp;SUBSEQUENT EVENTS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Management&#8217;s Evaluation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Management has evaluated subsequent events through November 4, 2026, the date the consolidated financial statements were available to be issued and no other material events require disclosure except the following:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On January 10, 2026, the Company issued 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock for a commitment fee in connection with the Share Purchase Agreement described in Note 14.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On January 10, 2026, the Company issued 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock pursuant to Real Property Purchase Agreement as described in Note 4.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>On February 19, 2026, the Company&#8217;s CEO provided a cash advance of $3,500 to the Company for working capital. &nbsp;The amount is non-interest bearing, unsecured and due on demand.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>On March 10, 2026, the Company&#8217;s CEO provided a cash advance of $50,000 to the Company for working capital. The amount is non-interest bearing, unsecured and due on demand.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>On April 8, 2026, the Company&#8217;s CEO provided a cash advance of $30,000 to the Company for working capital. &nbsp;The amount is non-interest bearing, unsecured and due on demand.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>On June 26, 2026, the Company issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share to the CEO of the Company to settle debt of $315,421 due to a company controlled by the CEO of the Company, of which $5 was forgiven and treated as a contribution to the Company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>On November 2, 2026, the Company and Silver Rock Group Ltd entered into Amendment No. 1 to the Share Purchase Agreement described in Note 14, which confirms the aggregate purchase commitment of $350,000,000, provides that the number of shares of Class A Common Stock registered for resale by Silver Rock under any single registration statement shall not exceed 29.99% of the shares then outstanding, provides that the Company shall not issue shares to Silver Rock under the agreement and the related warrants (including the 2,178,656 commitment shares) in excess of 19.99% of the shares outstanding immediately prior to the Public Listing unless stockholder approval is obtained, and fixes the warrant exercise price on the Public Listing date without subsequent reset.</P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:11pt><B>Biointra, Corp.</B></FONT></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><B>Notes to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:9pt><B>For the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025</B></FONT></P>

<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:3pt'><FONT style=font-size:9pt><B>(unaudited)</B></FONT></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 1 &#8211;&nbsp;NATURE OF OPERATIONS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Biointra, Corp. was incorporated in Delaware on May 8, 2024 (the &#8220;Company&#8221;). The Company is in the business of developing integrated solutions for the recovery and beneficial use of organic waste, including renewable-energy-related initiatives, with operations concentrated in Mexico. In connection with this strategy, through its wholly owned subsidiary, the Company acquired agricultural properties in Mexico that include land, agricultural improvements, water rights, buildings, and avocado and blue agave bearer plants. These properties are under active cultivation. The agricultural operations are intended to preserve and develop the productive value of the acquired properties and provide operational flexibility and potential agricultural inputs and cash flows while the Company continues to develop its broader renewable-energy and organic-waste recovery initiatives.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>To date, the Company&#8217;s activities have principally consisted of raising capital, organizational matters, development of its business plan, and activities related to the acquired agricultural properties. The Company has not generated revenue since inception.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 2 &#8211;&nbsp;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Basis of Presentation and Principles of Consolidation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The accounting and reporting policies of the Company conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). In the opinion of management, all adjustments considered necessary for the fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements for the periods presented have been included. The Company&#8217;s fiscal year end is December 31.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Biointra Renovables Atotonilco Jalisco SAPI DE CV (&#8220;BRA&#8221;). All inter-company transactions and balances have been eliminated upon consolidation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Interim Financial Statements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The accompanying unaudited interim consolidated financial statements of the Company have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;US GAAP&#8221;) and the rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;), and should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements and notes thereto. In the opinion of management, all adjustments, consisting of normal recurring adjustments, necessary for a fair presentation of financial position and the results of operations for the interim periods presented have been reflected herein. The results of operations for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of the results to be expected for the full year. Notes to the financial statements which would substantially duplicate the disclosure contained in the audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year end December 31, 2025, have been omitted.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Use of Estimates</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and the footnotes thereto. Actual results could differ from those estimates. It is reasonably possible that changes in estimates will occur in the near term. All amounts are rounded to the nearest whole dollar upon presentation so certain sums or differences may reflect a rounding difference in some instances.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Examples of reported amounts that rely on significant estimates include certain amounts relating to the accounting for acquired agricultural property and equipment, inventory, income taxes, including valuation allowance, and stock-based compensation expense.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Risks and Uncertainties</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has a limited operating history. The Company&#8217;s business and operations are sensitive to general business and economic conditions in the United States and Mexico. A host of factors beyond the Company&#8217;s control could cause fluctuations </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-22</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>in these conditions. Adverse conditions may include: recession, downturn or otherwise, local market competition, changing consumer preferences, unpredictable climate patterns, and agricultural yield volatility. These adverse conditions could affect the Company&#8217;s financial condition and the results of its operations. As of June 30, 2026, the Company is operating as a going concern. See Note 12 for additional information.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Agricultural Operations</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company accounts for its agricultural activities in accordance with ASC 905, Agriculture. The Company&#8217;s agricultural properties, held through BRA, include avocado orchards and blue agave plantations. Avocado trees are perennial bearer plants: fruit is harvested annually and the trees remain in production over multiple growing seasons. Blue agave is harvested once, generally six to eight years after planting, and harvest of the agave heart removes the plant.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'><B>Bearer plants. </B>The avocado trees acquired with the agricultural properties were recorded at the amounts allocated to them in the asset acquisition described in Note 4 and are presented within property and equipment as bearer plants (Note 7). Bearer plants are depreciated on a straight-line basis over an estimated useful life of four years and are reviewed for impairment in accordance with the Company&#8217;s policy for long-lived assets. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'><B>Growing crops. </B>Costs incurred to cultivate the agave plants established by the Company after the acquisition date, including land preparation, plant material, fertilization, irrigation, pest control and direct labor, are accumulated as growing crops within inventories and charged to cost of sales when the related products are sold. General costs of maintaining the plantations that cannot be identified with a specific crop are expensed as incurred.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'><B>Harvested crops. </B>Harvested agricultural products held for sale are stated at the lower of cost and net realizable value.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>As of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, the Company held growing crops, no harvested crops or other agricultural inventory, and no sales of agricultural products were recorded in the periods presented.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Recent Accounting Pronouncements Not Yet Adopted</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, <I>Income Statement &#8211;&nbsp;Reporting Comprehensive Income &#8211;&nbsp;Expense Disaggregation Disclosure (Subtopic 220-40)</I>. The amendments in this update enhance disclosures about a public business entity&#8217;s expenses and provide more detailed information about the types of expenses included in certain notes in the consolidated financial statements. ASU 2024-03 is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and interim reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2027. Early adoption permitted. The amendments may be applied prospectively to reporting periods after the effective date or retrospectively to all periods presented in the consolidated financial statements. The Company is currently evaluating any new disclosures that may be required upon adoption of ASU 2024-03.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company&#8217;s management does not believe that any recently issued, but not yet effective, accounting standards, if currently adopted, would have a material effect on the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 3 &#8211;&nbsp;ACQUISITION OF BIOINTRA RENOVABLES ATOTONILCO JALISCO SAPI DE CV</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On April 22, 2025, the Company entered into a Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA, a Mexican corporation controlled by the CEO of the Company. Pursuant to the agreement, the Company issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company on May 6, 2025 to acquire all of the outstanding shares of BRA. The Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement closed upon the Company obtaining control of BRA on August 8, 2025. Pursuant to ASC 805-50-30-5, the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition under common control. The transfer of the net assets or equity interest from BRA does not constitute a business and therefore would not represent a change in the reporting entity. At the closing of the acquisition, the Company recognized the net assets of BRA at the historical carrying value of $421 and began reporting the net assets transferred in its consolidated financial statements prospectively from the date of the transfer. The difference between the fair value of shares of Class A Common Stock issued and the net assets or equity interests of BRA is included in additional paid-in capital at June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 4 &#8211;&nbsp;REAL PROPERTY PURCHASE AGREEMENT</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On September 15, 2025, BRA entered into a Real Property Purchase Agreement to acquire certain agricultural property assets which consists of land, land improvements, water licenses and avocado and agave plantations including buildings and bearer plants, with a fair value of $5,426,066 (MXN99,652,094) in consideration for 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company. The fair value of the consideration payable was determined based on third-party appraisals of assets acquired along with observable market data from transactions between normal market participants. BRA obtained control of the agricultural property assets upon execution of the Real Property Purchase Agreement, and the agricultural property is currently </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-23</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>under active cultivation with developing crops. On February 22, 2026, the Company issued the 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock. Refer to Note 6, Note 7 and Note 8 for the details of assets acquired in the transaction.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 5 &#8211;&nbsp;DEFERRED FINANCING COSTS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>During the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company recorded $10,000 of deferred financing costs related to its planned S-1 registration statement.</P>

<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 9 &#8211;&nbsp;STOCKHOLDERS&#8217; DEFICIT</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Common Stock</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has 3 classes of Common Stock; Class A, Class B and Class C.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 800,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has 123,650,883 Class A Common Stock outstanding as of June 30, 2026 (December 31, 2025 &#8211;&nbsp;119,932,800). Each Class A Common Stock is entitled to 1 vote per share.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 50,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has 10,000,000 Class B Common Stock outstanding as of June 30, 2026 (December 31, 2025 &#8211;&nbsp;10,000,000). Each Class B Common Stock is entitled to 20 votes per share.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has authorized 75,000,000 Class C Common Stock (par value $0.000001). The Company has not issued any Class C Common Stock as of June 30, 2026. Shares of Class C Common Stock have no voting power.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><I>During the six months ended June 30, 2026:</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On February 22, 2026, the Company issued 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock for a commitment fee in connection with the Share Purchase Agreement described in Note 13.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On February 22, 2026, the Company issued 1,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock pursuant to the Real Property Purchase Agreement as described in Note 4.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On June 26, 2026, the Company issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share to the CEO of the Company in settlement of related party debt of $315,421 (Note 10). The shares were issued and outstanding as at June 30, 2026.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><I>During the six months ended June 30, 2025:</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On May 6, 2025, the Company issued 5,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock of the Company pursuant to the Share Exchange and Acquisition Agreement with BRA dated April 22, 2025. The Company obtained control of BRA on August 8, 2025, and, because the transaction was an asset acquisition under common control, the net assets of BRA were recorded at their historical carrying value of $421 rather than at the fair value of the shares issued (Note 3).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On May 6, 2025, the Company issued 6,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at a fair value of $600,000 for services to be rendered for the period from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026. During the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company recorded consulting expense of $100,000 and $250,000, respectively (2025 - $50,000 and $50,000, respectively) on the statements of operations and comprehensive loss.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Preferred Stock</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company has 75,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock authorized with a par value of $0.000001, as of the filing date of these statements. As at June 30, 2026, there are no shares of Preferred Stock issued or outstanding. The Company&#8217;s board of directors have not yet authorized the rights and privileges of the Preferred Stock.</P>

<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 10 &#8211;&nbsp;RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS AND BALANCES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>All transactions with related parties have occurred in the normal course of operations and are recorded at the exchange amount which is the amount agreed to by the Company and the related parties.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt'>As at June 30, 2026, the Company owed $35,441 (December 31, 2025 - $224,274) to a company controlled by the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) of the Company which represents cash advances, deferred financing costs, prepaid consulting fees, and general and administrative expenses incurred on behalf of the Company. The amount is non-interest bearing, unsecured and due on demand. &nbsp;On June 26, 2026, the Company issued 39,427 shares of Class A Common Stock at $8.00 per share to the CEO of the Company to settle debt of $315,421 due to a company controlled by the CEO of the Company, of which $5 was forgiven and treated as a contribution to the Company. &nbsp;</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 11 &#8211;&nbsp;SEGMENT REPORTING</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company views its operations and manages its business as one operating and reporting segment. This single segment reflects the Company&#8217;s core business, which is the development of solutions to recycle organic waste for the production of renewable energy, and is operated in two geographical areas (U.S.A. and Mexico).</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company&#8217;s Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;), who is the Chief Executive Officer, evaluates financial performance and allocates resources on a consolidated basis. The CODM uses consolidated operating loss, net loss, and cash flow information to assess performance and make decisions regarding the allocation of resources. As these financial measures are reviewed on a consolidated basis, the Company has determined that it has a single operating and reporting segment.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>The Company operates in two geographical areas of U.S.A. and Mexico. The Company&#8217;s property and equipment, and intangible assets, and all related depreciation and amortization, by geographical areas as at June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, were all located in Mexico.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 12 &#8211;&nbsp;GOING CONCERN</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>These consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles applicable to a going concern, which assumes that the Company will be able to meet its obligations and continue its operations for a period of at least one year from the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements. Realization values may be substantially different from carrying values as shown and these consolidated financial statements do not give effect to adjustments that would be necessary to the carrying values and classification of assets and liabilities should the Company be unable to continue as a going concern. At June 30, 2026, the Company had not yet achieved profitable operations and expects to incur further losses in the development of its business. As reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements, the Company had an accumulated deficit of $1,785,401 at June 30, 2026. This factor among others raises substantial doubt about the Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. The Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern is dependent upon its ability to generate future profitable operations and/or to obtain the necessary financing to meet its obligations and repay its liabilities arising from normal business operations when they come due. Management has no formal plan in place to address this concern but considers that the Company will be able to obtain additional funds by equity financing and/or related party advances, however, there is no assurance of additional funding being available.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 13 &#8211;&nbsp;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Share Purchase Agreement</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On August 29, 2024, the Company entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Silver Rock Group (&#8220;Silver Rock&#8221;) whereby Silver Rock committed to purchase up to $350,000,000 of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock (the &#8220;Draw Down Amount&#8221;) over a 36-month period beginning on the date the Company becomes publicly listed (&#8220;Public Listing&#8221;). The agreement provides the Company with the right, at its sole discretion, to issue Draw Down Notices in tranches of up to one million shares at a per-share price equal to a 10% discount to the lowest trading price of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock during the 10 trading days immediately preceding the Draw Down Notice. The Draw Down Amount requested shall not exceed 200% or one million dollars of the average daily trading volume for the 10 trading days immediately preceding the draw down exercise date on a rolling basis.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In connection with the Share Purchase Agreement, the Company agreed to pay a commitment fee equal to 2% of the total outstanding shares of the Company on the date of the agreement. During the period ended December 31, 2024, the Company recorded a commitment fee of $217,866 on the statement of operations and comprehensive loss for 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock. On February 22, 2026, the Company issued 2,178,656 shares of Class A Common Stock.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><FONT style=font-size:9pt>F-26</FONT></P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#0000A0;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>In addition, on the date of Public Listing, the Company shall issue share purchase warrants to Silver Rock granting the right to purchase additional common shares of the Company for a period of 5 years at an exercise price per share equal to the lower of $2 per share or 110% of the listing price immediately after the Public Listing. The number of warrants issued shall be equal to 4% of the total outstanding shares immediately after the completion of the Public Listing, calculated on a fully diluted basis. As at June 30, 2026 and the issuance date of the consolidated financial statements, the Company has not become publicly listed. As a result, the number of warrants to be issued and its fair value are indeterminable.</P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:5pt;color:#000000'><B>NOTE 14 &#8211;&nbsp;SUBSEQUENT EVENTS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:7pt;margin-bottom:4pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Management&#8217;s Evaluation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>Management has evaluated subsequent events through November 4, 2026, the date the condensed consolidated financial statements were available to be issued, and has determined that, other than as described below, no events or transactions have occurred after June 30, 2026 that require recognition or disclosure in these condensed consolidated financial statements.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:5pt'>On November 2, 2026, the Company and Silver Rock entered into Amendment No. 1 to the Share Purchase Agreement described in Note 13, which confirms the aggregate purchase commitment of $350,000,000, provides that the number of Class A Common Stock registered for resale by Silver Rock under any single registration statement shall not exceed 29.99% of the shares then outstanding, and provides that the Company shall not issue shares to Silver Rock under the agreement and the related warrants (including the 2,178,656 commitment shares) in excess of 19.99% of the shares outstanding immediately prior to the Public Listing unless stockholder approval is obtained.</P>
